Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 14, verses 1–4 (part 1 of 2):

Now, the first part of the surah.

Lesson No. 114: Commentary on verses
1 to 27
Verses 1 to 4

Alif-Lam-Ra. (14:1) "O Muhammad, this is a Book which We have sent down to you." This Book is composed of the letters Alif, Lam, Mim and other similar letters. We have sent it down to you; no one else has sent it down to you, nor have you yourself composed it. And why it has been sent down.

Li-tukhrija an-nas min adh-dhulumati ila an-nur (14:1) "That you may bring mankind out of darkness into light." You are to bring the whole of humanity out of darkness into light. You are to bring the whole of humanity out of darkness into light. The darknesses of superstition and fabrication, the darknesses of inherited customs and traditions, the darknesses of serving many lords, of conflict and bewilderment, the darknesses of Jahili values, standards, and Jahili ideas and conceptions: from these you are to extract humanity and bring it into the light of the Quran. It is a light which truly dispels all these darknesses. It illuminates the realm of conscience and brings radiance to the field of thought and vision. It brings radiance to the practical paths of life and to life's lofty purposes and lofty ideas.

Faith in Allah is a light by which the heart is illuminated, and when a person's heart is illuminated, his entire personality and his human frame are also made luminous, and both aspects of the human personality, the clay and the spirit of Allah, both become illuminated. But when a human personality is emptied of this light, and the lamp is extinguished within him, then man is a heap of dark clay and a mire in the form of blood and flesh, because flesh and blood are wholly composed of the material elements of the earth. If this light, which flows from the spirit of Allah, were not present, and within it faith did not exist in its pure, polished form, then through it this black matter becomes transparent and shining, and then this black mire becomes a transparent mirror.

The truth is that faith in Allah is a light by which the human self shines. In its illumination a person can determine his path. He sees the path to Allah perfectly clear. In this path there is neither haze nor dust: the dust of superstition, the dust of greed and desires. And when the human self sees the path and it appears clearly, then in such a path there is no stumbling, no agitation, no hesitation, and no bewilderment.

Then, firm faith in Allah is a light by which the whole of life is illuminated. All people are equal servants of Allah. The bond among them is a bond of divinity. They worship and obey Allah alone. Now there is no division of master and slave among them. They gain recognition of this entire universe and they are connected to this entire universe. They see and know that this whole universe runs according to the divine order and the law of nature, so they come into harmony with this universe and with all the creatures within it, because all of them are creatures of Allah.

Then faith is a light, a light of justice, a light of freedom, a light of knowledge and recognition, a light of love for Allah, a light of trust in the justice, wisdom and mercy of Allah. Whether there are hardships or joys, this faith inclines a person to patience in hardships, teaches gratitude to the Lord in joys, and bestows wisdom and experience in trials.

Faith in Allah alone, that He is the deity and Lord, is also a system of life. It is not merely a creed and a concept that illuminates the heart. This system of life is founded solely on the principle of serving Allah alone. In it there is belief in the Lordship of Allah alone and rejection of all other lordships. Within it, greatness befits that unique Being alone. He alone is the Sovereign, and all are His servants.

In this system of life there is harmony with human nature; it takes into account the essential and indispensable needs of man, needs which lead him to felicity, give him the light of tranquility, and bestow upon him joy and happiness. In this system there is also stability and permanence, and man is protected from the changes, upheavals, bewilderments and anxieties that exist in societies which worship other human beings besides Allah. In it no human being is the ruler of another human being. In politics, in government, in economics, and in the collective relations and customs of society, no human being is the slave of another human being. In this system the powers of human beings are not spent on making other human beings slaves, nor in it is any person a drummer for some tyrannical power.

Within this brief phrase, "that you may bring people from darkness to light" (14:1), lie hidden vast meanings and great truths, which can become visible as a result of deep reflection of heart and sight. Those horizons can become visible only after the establishment of the Islamic system of life. Mere human words are not sufficient to express these vast meanings.

Bi-idhni rabbihim (14:1) "By the permission of their Lord, to bring them from darkness into light." By the command of Allah and by His permission alone can you accomplish this task, because the duty of the Messenger is only to convey the message. His responsibility is only to explain. As for people coming from darkness into light, this can happen only by Allah's grace and bounty, by His command and permission, and this work proceeds in accordance with the Sunnah which operates in harmony with Allah's will. The Messenger is only a Messenger.

Ila sirati al-'Aziz al-Hamid (14:1) "To the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy God." Grammatically, "sirat" is in apposition to "an-nur," and the path of Allah is the way of Allah, the Sunnah of Allah, His order which governs this entire universe. His path is His Shari'ah, which has been sent to dominate life, and the light of faith guides towards that Shari'ah. Rather, this light itself is that path and Shari'ah. The faith-light that shines within the human self shines also throughout this entire universe. This is the divine Sunnah, the order of nature, and it is that Shari'ah. Whoever's self is illuminated by this light does not commit error in perception and conception; he does not err in conduct and way of life either. This is the straight path. The way of the Mighty and Praiseworthy is this, and He is the Mighty, the possessor of overpowering might, and Praiseworthy in His own essence, and dominant over the entire universe.

Here the manifestation of Allah's power is mentioned so that the disbelievers may be somewhat frightened upon hearing it, and "Praiseworthy" is mentioned so that the grateful may praise Him and give thanks to Him. After this it is said that He is also the owner and ruler of the heavens and the earth. He has no need of people; He holds this entire universe in His power.

Allahi alladhi lahu ma fi as-samawati wa ma fi al-ard (14:2) "Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth." As for the one who has come out of darkness into light and attained the guidance, here silence is maintained about him. Here a warning is given to those who refuse to come into the light. The disbelievers are warned of severe punishment because they rejected the benefit of this blessing. What greater blessing could there be than that Allah sent a Messenger and gave him a Book, so that he might bring people out of darkness into light? This is so great a blessing that no human being can fully give thanks for this supreme blessing. But if someone, on the contrary, is ungrateful for this blessing, then it is said:

Wa-wailun lil-kafirina min 'adhabin shadid (14:2) "And woe to the disbelievers because of a severe punishment," meaning, for those who refuse to accept the truth. Here it is explained what quality it is that constitutes ingratitude and disbelief toward this blessing which the noble Messenger has brought. That quality is:

Alladhina yastahibbuna al-hayata ad-dunya 'ala al-akhirati wa yasuddDuna 'an sabili Allahi wa yabghunaha 'iwajan ula'ika fi dalalin ba'id (14:3) "Those who prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter, who bar others from the way of Allah and seek to make it crooked, these are people who have gone far astray." The love of the world over the Hereafter is in conflict with the requirements of faith and is contrary to steadfastness upon the straight path. When someone prefers the Hereafter over the world, the situation does not remain as it is. Preferring the Hereafter also produces moderation in this world, and produces the fear of God in this world. Therefore, love and preference for the Hereafter does not necessitate renunciation of the world.

The reality is that those whose hearts turn toward the Hereafter are not losers in the field of the world either. This notion occurs only to those whose thinking has deviated from the path of moderation. In Islam, the concept of preferring the Hereafter is in fact for the reform of this world itself. Among the requirements of faith in Allah is the important requirement that the duty of vicegerency on earth be carried out in the best and most beautiful manner. The right of earthly vicegerency includes taking interest in the building and development of the earth and benefiting from the treasures within it. In Islam there is no concept that the order of worldly life should be suspended for the benefit of the Hereafter; rather, the building and development of life for the sake of truth, justice, righteousness and the pleasure of God is itself the preparation for the development of the Hereafter. It is the policy of Islam that there be good in this world and good in the Hereafter.

Now, who are those who prefer this world over the Hereafter? They are people who cannot reach their vile objectives in the light of faith. They can decide upon the natural resources and issues of the earth only in such a way, they can earn unlawful wealth only in such a way, they can exploit people only in such a way, and they can plunder the collective wealth of people only when they step outside the circle of the light of faith and are deprived of guidance to the religion of Allah and steadfastness upon it. That is why such worldly-minded people also bar others from the path of Allah, and they themselves do not walk on the path of Allah; rather, they seek to mold the religion and Shari'ah of Allah according to their own whims. They wish to remove steadfastness and justice from religion and justice from economics. When these people succeed in barring themselves and other common people from the way of Allah, and when they release themselves from the justice and steadfastness of Islam, then, and only then, can such people oppress, rebel, deceive, and incite people to corruption. In this way they again take control of the resources of the earth, earn unlawful wealth, and amass wealth through degrading and immoral means. Then they adopt rebellion and arrogance upon the earth. They make people slaves and reduce people to such weakness that they no longer have the strength to resist or protest.

It is a fact that the faith-based system of life is in truth the guarantor of life, dignity and economic justice, and it is also the guarantee that the influence of those who wish to seize the resources of the earth, or who wish to promote worldliness over the Hereafter, will be brought to an end.

Wa ma arsalna min ... lahum (14:4) "And We never sent a Messenger except with the language of his people, so that he might explain clearly to them." This has been a great blessing for mankind in the prophethood of every Prophet: that the Messenger was sent in their own language, so that he could bring people out of darkness into light with great ease. It was also necessary that he be a speaker of their language, so that he could explain, they could understand, and the purpose would be fulfilled.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was also sent as a Messenger in the language of his people. Although he was a Messenger for all of humanity, because the responsibility was placed upon his people that now the duty of conveying this message to all of humanity rests with the Arabs. The lifespan of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was limited. The responsibility placed upon him was that he first purify the Arabian Peninsula from jahiliyyah and make Islam dominant there, so that it would become the center and source, and that his message and call would then be carried by the community to far distant lands. And indeed this is what happened: when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had made Islam dominant in the Arabian Peninsula, Allah took him from this world. However, the Messenger himself had prepared the Army of Usama for the outskirts of the Arabian Peninsula; this army had not yet departed when the Messenger ﷺ passed away. Before this, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had sent his letters of invitation to other countries beyond the Arabian Peninsula. He sent these letters so that people would see that his prophethood was for all of mankind. But Allah had appointed for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ only this duty, and within the short human lifespan a single person can do only this: that he carry out the work of preaching in the Arabian Peninsula in the Arabic language, and after that the work of conveying the message to the whole world be carried out later by the bearers of the Islamic call. And so it happened. Therefore there is no contradiction in the fact that the prophethood of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was for all of humanity, while he himself was to work in his national language and, during his lifetime, to work practically among the Arabs.

Then Allah leaves astray whomever He wills, and guides whomever He wills. And He is the Mighty, the Wise. (14:4)

The duty of every Messenger and every Prophet, including the final Prophet of the Last Age, is only this: to convey his message. As for whether a person takes the path of guidance or not, this is not within the power of any Messenger. It is Allah's work to guide someone or to let him go astray. Even the Messenger's own wish in this matter does not necessarily have to be fulfilled. This is the prerogative of Allah. He has established for this a sunnah (a fixed law or pattern) in this universe. This sunnah operates in accordance with Allah's will. Whoever adopts the means of straying and takes the path of error becomes astray, and whoever adopts the means of guidance and embraces the ways of guidance becomes one of the people of guidance. All these matters occur in accordance with and subject to Allah's will. And for humankind, Allah has laid down this sunnah.

﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ (14:4) He has the power to transform the lives of people in whatever way He wills, and He exercises this control through His wisdom and His decree. Allah has taken all affairs under His control. In His dominion, events do not occur by chance, without any cause, and without any plan.

In this system the powers of human beings are not spent on making other human beings slaves, nor in it is any person a drummer for some tyrannical power.

Within this brief phrase, "that you may bring people from darkness to light" (14:1), lie hidden vast meanings and great truths, which can become visible as a result of deep reflection of heart and sight. Those horizons can become visible only after the establishment of the Islamic system of life. Mere human words are not sufficient to express these vast meanings.

Bi-idhni rabbihim (14:1) "By the permission of their Lord, to bring them from darkness into light." By the command of Allah and by His permission alone can you accomplish this task, because the duty of the Messenger is only to convey the message. His responsibility is only to explain. As for people coming from darkness into light, this can happen only by Allah's grace and bounty, by His command and permission, and this work proceeds in accordance with the Sunnah which operates in harmony with Allah's will. The Messenger is only a Messenger.

Ila sirati al-'Aziz al-Hamid (14:1) "To the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy God." Grammatically, "sirat" is in apposition to "an-nur," and the path of Allah is the way of Allah, the Sunnah of Allah, His order which governs this entire universe. His path is His Shari'ah, which has been sent to dominate life, and the light of faith guides towards that Shari'ah. Rather, this light itself is that path and Shari'ah. The faith-light that shines within the human self shines also throughout this entire universe. This is the divine Sunnah, the order of nature, and it is that Shari'ah. Whoever's self is illuminated by this light does not commit error in perception and conception; he does not err in conduct and way of life either. This is the straight path. The way of the Mighty and Praiseworthy is this, and He is the Mighty, the possessor of overpowering might, and Praiseworthy in His own essence, and dominant over the entire universe.

Here the manifestation of Allah's power is mentioned so that the disbelievers may be somewhat frightened upon hearing it, and "Praiseworthy" is mentioned so that the grateful may praise Him and give thanks to Him. After this it is said that He is also the owner and ruler of the heavens and the earth. He has no need of people; He holds this entire universe in His power.

As for the one who has come out of darkness into light and attained the guidance, here silence is maintained about him. Here a warning is given to those who refuse to come into the light. The disbelievers are warned of severe punishment because they rejected the benefit of this blessing. What greater blessing could there be than that Allah sent a Messenger and gave him a Book, so that he might bring people out of darkness into light? This is so great a blessing that no human being can fully give thanks for this supreme blessing. But if someone, on the contrary, is ungrateful for this blessing, then it is said:

Wa-wailun lil-kafirina min 'adhabin shadid (14:2) "And woe to the disbelievers because of a severe punishment," meaning, for those who refuse to accept the truth. Here it is explained what quality it is that constitutes ingratitude and disbelief toward this blessing which the noble Messenger has brought. That quality is:

Alladhina yastahibbuna al-hayata ad-dunya 'ala al-akhirati wa yasuddDuna 'an sabili Allahi wa yabghunaha 'iwajan ula'ika fi dalalin ba'id (14:3) "Those who prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter, who bar others from the way of Allah and seek to make it crooked, these are people who have gone far astray." The love of the world over the Hereafter is in conflict with the requirements of faith and is contrary to steadfastness upon the straight path. When someone prefers the Hereafter over the world, the situation does not remain as it is. Preferring the Hereafter also produces moderation in this world, and produces the fear of God in this world. Therefore, love and preference for the Hereafter does not necessitate renunciation of the world.

The reality is that those whose hearts turn toward the Hereafter are not losers in the field of the world either. This notion occurs only to those whose thinking has deviated from the path of moderation. In Islam, the concept of preferring the Hereafter is in fact for the reform of this world itself. Among the requirements of faith in Allah is the important requirement that the duty of vicegerency on earth be carried out in the best and most beautiful manner. The right of earthly vicegerency includes taking interest in the building and development of the earth and benefiting from the treasures within it. In Islam there is no concept that the order of worldly life should be suspended for the benefit of the Hereafter; rather, the building and development of life for the sake of truth, justice, righteousness and the pleasure of God is itself the preparation for the development of the Hereafter. It is the policy of Islam that there be good in this world and good in the Hereafter.

Now, who are those who prefer this world over the Hereafter? They are people who cannot reach their vile objectives in the light of faith. They can decide upon the natural resources and issues of the earth only in such a way, they can earn unlawful wealth only in such a way, they can exploit people only in such a way, and they can plunder the collective wealth of people only when they step outside the circle of the light of faith and are deprived of guidance to the religion of Allah and steadfastness upon it. That is why such worldly-minded people also bar others from the path of Allah, and they themselves do not walk on the path of Allah; rather, they seek to mold the religion and Shari'ah of Allah according to their own whims. They wish to remove steadfastness and justice from religion and justice from economics. When these people succeed in barring themselves and other common people from the way of Allah, and when they release themselves from the justice and steadfastness of Islam, then, and only then, can such people oppress, rebel, deceive, and incite people to corruption. In this way they again take control of the resources of the earth, earn unlawful wealth, and amass wealth through degrading and immoral means. Then they adopt rebellion and arrogance upon the earth. They make people slaves and reduce people to such weakness that they no longer have the strength to resist or protest.

It is a fact that the faith-based system of life is in truth the guarantor of life, dignity and economic justice, and it is also the guarantee that the influence of those who wish to seize the resources of the earth, or who wish to promote worldliness over the Hereafter, will be brought to an end.

Wa ma arsalna min ... lahum (14:4) "And We never sent a Messenger except with the language of his people, so that he might explain clearly to them." This has been a great blessing for mankind in the prophethood of every Prophet: that the Messenger was sent in their own language, so that he could bring people out of darkness into light with great ease. It was also necessary that he be a speaker of their language, so that he could explain, they could understand, and the purpose would be fulfilled.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was also sent as a Messenger in the language of his people. Although he was a Messenger for all of humanity, because the responsibility was placed upon his people that now the duty of conveying this message to all of humanity rests with the Arabs. The lifespan of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was limited. The responsibility placed upon him was that he first purify the Arabian Peninsula from jahiliyyah and make Islam dominant there, so that it would become the center and source, and that his message and call would then be carried by the community to far distant lands. And indeed this is what happened: when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had made Islam dominant in the Arabian Peninsula, Allah took him from this world. However, the Messenger himself had prepared the Army of Usama for the outskirts of the Arabian Peninsula; this army had not yet departed when the Messenger ﷺ passed away. Before this, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had sent his letters of invitation to other countries beyond the Arabian Peninsula. He sent these letters so that people would see that his prophethood was for all of mankind. But Allah had appointed for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ only this duty, and within the short human lifespan a single person can do only this: that he carry out the work of preaching in the Arabian Peninsula in the Arabic language, and after that the work of conveying the message to the whole world be carried out later by the bearers of the Islamic call. And so it happened. Therefore there is no contradiction in the fact that the prophethood of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was for all of humanity, while he himself was to work in his national language and, during his lifetime, to work practically among the Arabs.

Then Allah leaves astray whomever He wills, and guides whomever He wills. And He is the Mighty, the Wise. (14:4)

The duty of every Messenger and every Prophet, including the final Prophet of the Last Age, is only this: to convey his message. As for whether a person takes the path of guidance or not, this is not within the power of any Messenger. It is Allah's work to guide someone or to let him go astray. Even the Messenger's own wish in this matter does not necessarily have to be fulfilled. This is the prerogative of Allah. He has established for this a sunnah (a fixed law or pattern) in this universe. This sunnah operates in accordance with Allah's will. Whoever adopts the means of straying and takes the path of error becomes astray, and whoever adopts the means of guidance and embraces the ways of guidance becomes one of the people of guidance. All these matters occur in accordance with and subject to Allah's will. And for humankind, Allah has laid down this sunnah.

﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ (14:4) He has the power to transform the lives of people in whatever way He wills, and He exercises this control through His wisdom and His decree. Allah has taken all affairs under His control. In His dominion, events do not occur by chance, without any cause, and without any plan.

Now, the first part of the surah.

Lesson No. 114: Commentary on verses
1 to 27

And when the human self sees the path and it appears clearly, then in such a path there is no stumbling, no agitation, no hesitation, and no bewilderment.

Thus We also sent Musa (peace be upon him) with the language of his people.

Verses 5 to 8

The command given to the Prophet (ﷺ) and the command given to Musa (peace be upon him) are worded identically. This surah adopts this same style of speech. We have already discussed this phrase in detail, and the explanation here is the same. This was the command for Muhammad (ﷺ):

﴿That you may bring mankind out from darknesses into light﴾ (14:1). The same command was given to Musa (peace be upon him):

﴿And indeed We sent Musa ... to bring your people out from darknesses into light﴾ (14:5).

The command to the Messenger (ﷺ) is for all of humanity, while the command to Musa (peace be upon him) was only for his own people. But the purpose of both was one and the same: to bring their people out of darknesses.

﴿And remind them of the Days of Allah﴾ (14:5). All days belong to Allah, but here the historical days are meant, in which Allah's blessings or His punishment are clearly seen, so that humanity, or a particular community of humanity, may benefit from them and take admonition. The following details show that Musa (peace be upon him) warned his people about the Days of Allah (Ayyam Allah, the decisive days of Allah's dealings with nations), and reminded them of the historical events of peoples: the people of Nuh (Noah), the 'Ad, the Thamud, and the nations that came after them. These are the Days of Allah.

﴿Indeed in that are signs for everyone who is patient and grateful﴾ (14:5). Among these days, some are signs, proofs and tokens of the misfortune of nations, from which the lesson of patience is drawn, and some are signs of Allah's blessings, from which the lesson of gratitude is drawn. Only the person who is patient and who renders thanks can grasp these lessons and understand the wisdom and admonition within them. Moreover, they contain consolation and reminder for such a person.

Accordingly, Musa (peace be upon him) continued to discharge the duties of prophethood among his people and kept admonishing them.

﴿And [remember] when Musa said to his people: "Remember the favour of Allah upon you, when He delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who inflicted on you a terrible torment, slaughtering your sons and keeping your women alive. In that was a great trial from your Lord."﴾ (14:6)

Musa (peace be upon him) reminds them of the blessings of Allah. This blessing is that Allah rescued them from a severe punishment. This punishment was being inflicted on them by the family of Pharaoh, and it was continuously being inflicted upon them. There was no interval or holiday in it, and the extreme of this punishment was that they would kill the boys among their children and let the girls live. The reason was so that their capacity for resistance would not remain, and that, due to the shortage of men, they would become weak in war, so that they could be kept humiliated. Allah brought them out of this state of slavery and disgrace. Accordingly, Musa (peace be upon him) reminds them here of this so that they would render thanks.

﴿In that was a great trial from your Lord﴾ (14:6). First, they were tested not with blessing but with calamity, so that their patience, endurance, capacity for resistance and resolve would be tested, to see how sincere they were and how much they carried out the commands of Allah. The meaning of patience is not that a person endures humiliation until he becomes accustomed to it. Rather, patience is that a person bears hardships but his steadfastness does not waver. He does not accept defeat, does not lose heart spiritually, keeps his full resolve to pursue his own programme, and has within him the resolve to prepare to confront oppression and tyranny. If this is not the case, then it is not patience but accepting degradation and humiliation. Even in deliverance there is a trial for them: whether they give thanks or not, whether they acknowledge this blessing of Allah or not, and whether, in exchange for deliverance, they adopt the path of guidance of Allah or not.

Musa (peace be upon him) now continues further. After mentioning the Days of Allah, he now gives them instructions for the future and tells them that now they should make patience and gratitude their way of life, and that if they give thanks, the outcome will be good, but if they disbelieve, the punishment of Allah will again be prepared.

﴿And [remember] when your Lord proclaimed: "If you are grateful, I will surely increase you; but if you are ungrateful, indeed My punishment is severe."﴾ (14:7)

This is a great truth: that through gratitude for blessings, blessings increase, and through ingratitude for blessings, a person comes within the severe grasp of Allah. When we reflect on this truth, our hearts are at once satisfied with it, for on the one hand this is the true promise of Allah, and it must certainly be fulfilled. But if we also wish to learn its causes and seek causes that we can understand, we do not need to go very far.

From the fact of gratitude for blessings, it becomes clear that the one who gives thanks has a right standard settled within his soul. The natural demand of a blessing is that gratitude be rendered for it. Every sound nature considers gratitude the natural return for a favour. This is one cause. Secondly, the person who renders Allah's thanks for blessings believes that Allah alone is the disposer of these blessings. In this way, such a person refrains from rebellion, does not consider himself superior to people, and will not use the blessings of Allah to harm God's creatures, to cause mischief, to spread corruption in society, and especially to spread filth.

Through these matters, purity enters a person's soul, and such a person advances toward righteous deeds. He makes good use of the wealth given by God, and because of this good use, it grows and blessing comes into it. In this way, the people around such a person also become pleased with him, and because of that pleasure they assist him further. Thus a peaceful environment is provided for the development of the economy, and it grows. Although, for a believer, it is sufficient that if you give thanks I will give you more wealth, whether or not he can understand the other causes, because the promise of Allah is a truth and it must certainly be fulfilled.

The disbelief in Allah's blessings is of two kinds. One is that a blessing is not thanked for. The other is that a wealthy person denies that the Giver of these blessings is Allah. He attributes these blessings to his own knowledge, his own skill and his own personal effort. As if he thinks that knowledge, skill and the power of effort are not Allah's blessings, but are produced by himself. Ingratitude also takes the form that, because of them, this person becomes rebellious, becomes arrogant, considers himself a great thing compared to people, and spreads mischief through them, and indulges in luxury. All these matters come under ingratitude for the blessings of Allah.

The severe punishment also has various forms. Sometimes it comes in the way that the blessing of Allah is taken away from a person, and he is clearly deprived of it, or the effect that blessings have on human consciousness is wiped out. Sometimes a blessing is turned into a calamity for a person, and misfortunes come upon its possessor because of it. Those who are deprived of this blessing envy its possessor. And sometimes it happens that a punishment comes upon such a person in this world after a period, and sometimes this punishment is postponed until the Hereafter. But punishment certainly comes, because the crime of ingratitude for blessings cannot remain without punishment.

If someone gives thanks, it brings no benefit to Allah. And if someone is ungrateful for blessings, it brings no harm to Allah. Allah is Self-Sufficient (Ghani) and is in need of no one in either world. He is Praiseworthy (Hamid) in His own essence. It is not that He is praiseworthy only through the thanks and praise of people.

﴿And Musa said: "If you disbelieve, you and everyone on earth together, then indeed Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy."﴾ (14:8)

If you give thanks, your life will be set right through it. People's souls will turn toward Allah, will become pure, and through gratitude they will be set right. They will be content that this blessing, God willing, will continue, and there will be no fear of its deterioration or ending. Furthermore, the wealth spent as a thanksgiving for a blessing will not distress any soul, but will bring joy, because the Bestower is present, and the portion given as thanks purifies the remaining portion, and a greater reward will be gained.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 14, verse 9–11:

Verses 9 to 11

This admonition comes from the people of Musa (peace be upon him), but in the flow of the discourse the mention of Musa (peace be upon him) has been left out, so that the scene brings forward the messengers and their call as a whole. That is, despite differences of place and time, the attitude that all the messengers maintained toward the jahiliyyahs (ignorant systems) opposing them has been gathered together and brought into this scene. Musa (peace be upon him) is, as it were, the narrator presenting this great story. He has brought the major characters face to face within the story, and now they themselves take part in the conversation on the scene. This is a particular style of presenting narratives that the Qur'an has adopted: it presents a narrative and descriptive manner of speech in the form of living characters. We see that all the messengers and their peoples are present, and that the opposition of all the messengers is to jahiliyyahs. The distances of time and place between peoples and messengers are erased, and events are presented separated from time and place, whereas behind the veils of time and place lies the reality of existence.

﴿Has there not come to you the news of those before you: the people of Nuh, 'Ad, Thamud, and those after them, whose number none knows but Allah?﴾ (14:9) These are many peoples. Among them are some whose mention is not made in the Qur'an, that is, between the people of Musa and the people of Thamud. The purpose of the context here is not to give the details of these peoples, because the messengers are in reality one category, and the people to whom the call was being made are also one category.

﴿Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they put their hands to their mouths and said: "We disbelieve in what you have been sent with, and we are in grave doubt about that to which you invite us."﴾ (14:9)

The meaning of ﴿fa radd aydiyahum fi afwahihim﴾ (they put their hands to their mouths) is that just as a person places his hand before his mouth in order to raise his voice so that it is loud and can be heard at a distance, so people at that time would move the palm before their mouths so that by the forward and backward movement of the palm the voice would become louder. Thus more waves are produced in the voice, and because of this vibration the voice carries far. Here their action is presented because these people denied with forceful intensity. Openly and in an insulting manner, with the harshest and most ungracious methods devoid of decorum, they rejected the words of the messengers.

The fundamental point of the messengers' call was that Allah is One, that He alone is the Deity and Lord, and that none of His servants shares anything with Him. To doubt this truth, which every sound nature perceives and whose evidences spread visibly and manifestly throughout this universe, is in such circumstances an extremely reprehensible and foul act. The messengers regarded this doubt as profoundly abhorrent, since the system of the heavens and the earth is a witness that is just.

﴿Their messengers said: "Is there doubt about Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth?"﴾ (14:10) Is there doubt about Allah, when the system of the heavens and the earth proclaims with a loud voice that Allah is the One who created this system and sustains it? The messengers said this because the heavens and the earth are most clear and evident signs and proofs, and a mere indication toward them is sufficient. Any strayed person who observes their system can be brought onto the path of guidance. The messengers regarded a mere pointing to the heavens and the earth as sufficient. After this, the messengers began to enumerate Allah's blessings upon the servants: that He invited them to faith and granted them a period of respite so that they might reflect upon the call to guidance.

﴿He calls you that He may forgive you your sins﴾ (14:10). The true call is the call to faith, the outcome of which is forgiveness. Here, however, the call and forgiveness are brought together so that Allah's favour may be clearly manifest: that when people believe, forgiveness is granted. Then the attitude of these people and their stubborn rejection become all the more surprising and blameworthy, since they are invited to forgiveness and yet they put their hands into their mouths and deny.

﴿And gives you respite until an appointed term﴾ (14:10). Allah, while calling to faith and forgiveness, does not demand from them that they accept immediately, nor does He destroy them immediately after their denial, but grants respite. This respite lasts for a time in this world and may extend up to the Day of Resurrection. In this period you can reflect well upon this call, and also upon the majesty of Allah and the statements of the messengers. This is a great mercy and kindness of Allah, and it too is one of the blessings of Allah. So is this the answer that such blessings of Allah deserve, the answer you are giving? Yet these people are extremely ignorant, and they rely upon the same old ignorant objection.

﴿They said: "You are nothing but mortals like us. You wish to turn us away from what our fathers worshipped."﴾ (14:10) Allah sent a person from among humans as a messenger. This was an honour for humankind, but they neither understand it nor deny it, and not only do they doubt it, but they level the accusation against the messengers that they have plotted against us to turn us away from the path on which our fathers walked. But they do not reflect on why the messengers would wish to turn them away from that path. All idol-worshippers are always afflicted with intellectual stagnation, and their only argument is that our forefathers did this work. Yet they do not consider what the standing of the religion of the forefathers is. If reflection is employed, what is the standing of those deities? Instead of employing intellect and reason and accepting this new and reasonable call, these people demand proof from the messengers.

﴿So bring us a clear authority.﴾ (14:10) The messengers do not deny their humanity but affirm it; rather, they turn people's attention to the fact that Allah bestowed a favour upon them by making them fit to bear the burden of prophethood.

Thus more waves are produced in the voice, and because of this vibration the voice carries far. Here their action is presented because these people denied with forceful intensity. Verse 14:12

"And why should we not put our trust in Allah, when He has guided us in the ways of our lives?" This is the statement of one who holds firm conviction in his position and his method, who is content with his way, whose heart is filled with reliance upon his true Protector and Helper, and who believes that the One who gives guidance will also be his Helper and Supporter. If a traveller is on the right path, what does it matter to him whether he reaches the destination or not? The real concern should be whether the path on which the traveller is journeying is the path of da'wah or not.

The person who feels that the hand of Divine power is guiding him and leading him step by step is one whose consciousness cannot help but perceive the existence of Allah and His overpowering might. The heart of such a person is connected to Allah. The one who possesses this consciousness no longer hesitates to walk his path, even though there may be difficulties, and even though the greatest tyrannical powers may be sitting along the way. Therefore, here the Prophets (peace be upon them) are directed to this: that they should be certain that Allah is their Guide and Helper, and that they should pay no heed to the tyrannical powers, but walk their path fearlessly. They should rely upon Allah, pay no regard to the threats of the tyrannical powers, and simply press forward.

Only those people can reach this great truth who rise, in practice, with the Islamic movement against an established and firmly rooted sovereign tyrannical system. Only in the hearts of such practical people does the consciousness arise that Allah Himself is guiding them. They rely upon Allah, and their hearts are filled with faith and certainty. The hearts of such people feel that windows of light have opened for them, and through these windows and skylights there comes upon them a light, which is the light of faith. Through this connection, breezes of the fresh air of faith keep coming, and such hearts feel great intimacy and nearness with Allah. The workers of the Islamic movement in whose hearts this consciousness arises then pay no heed to the established tyrannical powers of this earth. No one can deceive them, and no one can frighten them. Such workers then look upon the power and authority of such tyrannical forces with utmost contempt, because their hearts are connected to Allah, and they no longer take into account the conspiracies and oppressions of these contemptible people.

"And why should we put our trust in Allah, when He has guided us in the ways of our lives?" "And we will be patient over the harm that you are inflicting upon us." We will exercise patience, and, Allah willing, our feet will never slip; we will not show weakness, our steps will not waver, weakness will not come near us, and we will not turn back on our heels. We will never deviate from this path in any direction, nor will we reduce our struggle, nor will we fall into doubt. And this is because:

﴿And upon Allah let the reliant put their trust﴾ (14:12). Now the rebellious tyrannical powers come fully into the open. These powers abandon argument and debate, and give up reflection, because they perceive that these people are iron chickpeas that cannot be chewed. Against ideas, these powers are defeated. Now they come forward with the crude weapons of violence, since the rebellious tyrannical powers have nothing else left to them.

This passage brings out the true nature of the struggle between Islam and jahiliyyah (the state of ignorance and rejection of divine guidance). No jahili system tolerates an independent Islamic sovereignty that stands outside its authority, even when that Islamic authority is willing to coexist peacefully with jahiliyyah. Jahiliyyah knows that Islam takes the form of an independent, dynamic society with its own leadership and its own distinct sphere, and this is precisely what no jahili order ever accepts.

So jahiliyyah does not merely demand that the messengers stop their call. It says: return to our creed and our party, merge into our jahili society, and melt away into our way of life, so that you no longer have any independent existence. This is exactly what the nature of the Islamic system does not accept, and the messengers do not abandon this position. They refuse, because a Muslim who has separated himself from jahili society cannot dissolve back into it.

The fact is that every jahili society is made up of elements that, by their very nature, reject any Islamic element, unless a Muslim devotes all his activist and practical energies to strengthening that jahili society and reinforcing the foundations of jahiliyyah. Some people mistakenly believe that they can serve Islam by entering jahiliyyah, dissolving into its system, and becoming a cog in its machine. Such people do not truly understand the constituent organs and the nature of Islamic society, nor do they understand the nature of jahili society. Every society accepts within itself only those elements that work for its own benefit and strengthen its position and system. This is why the messengers openly refuse, saying that they can no longer return to your creed and society. At this point, the overwhelming power of God strikes jahiliyyah again. It is a blow against which no force can stand, because it comes from a power of immense magnitude. Even great tyrants and dictators cannot withstand it.

It should be understood that the great power of God intervenes in matters of the movement only when the messengers have completely separated themselves from their people. They believe that God has delivered them from this jahiliyyah, and therefore they cannot return to its order. As long as they do not insist on their distinctive identity, as long as they do not persist in their religious creed and form their own separate society under their own leadership, and as long as this movement and leadership do not divide their people along ideological lines, God's great power does not intervene. In short, until a nation is divided into two communities, each with its own ideology, way of life, society and leadership, God's great power does not intervene. When the Islamic movement takes this position, God's great power strikes jahiliyyah with a decisive blow. Then all the taghut forces (tyrannical powers) that threaten the Islamic movement are shattered, and God establishes firmly on earth those people who are upright. Then God's promise is fulfilled, the promise He made to the messengers and to those who call to truth after them.

However, if the Islamic movement is part of jahili society, if it has dissolved within it, and if it works within the customs and organization of jahiliyyah without possessing a separate, distinct and independent movement or system and without its own leadership, then this intervention does not come, and God's help does not arrive.

﴿Then their Lord revealed to them: "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers."﴾ (14:13) Here the emphasis (the nun of emphasis) is used to express both certainty and grandeur. Both meanings carry great weight in this difficult situation. That is, We will destroy these oppressive polytheists, wrongdoers and rebels, because of their own corruption, because of the truth that was sent to the common people, and because of the fear and terror they had instilled among the people.

﴿And We will surely make you dwell in the land after them.﴾ (14:14) This is not a matter of partiality or of mere pleasantry. It is the continuous divine law (sunnah jariyah) of God, and God's judgments are always in accordance with justice.

﴿That is for whoever fears standing before Me and fears My threat.﴾ (14:14) That is, appointing one authority and then giving power and the vicegerency of the earth to another happens so that the rebels are removed and in their place a leadership that fears God is brought forward. Then that leadership does not transgress, does not act with arrogance or pride on earth, does not rule by tyranny and domination, fears God's limits, is accountable before God, and avoids corruption on earth. It does not oppress anyone on earth, because this authority has been granted to it on the basis that it is deemed worthy of it.

When there is complete separation between the people of truth and the people of falsehood, then against the lowly worldly power of the rebels and dictators, the great power of God appears as the Mighty, the Irresistible, the All-Encompassing. Because the mission of the messengers' preaching comes to an end, truth and falsehood stand arrayed against each other, and believers become distinguished from the liars. The situation then becomes this: on one side, in one camp, the power of the rebels of the world confronts them, while on the other side stand the messengers and the callers to truth, and with them is the great power of God. Both sides pray for victory and success, and the outcome unfolds accordingly.

Then that leadership does not transgress, does not act with arrogance or pride on earth, does not rule by tyranny and domination, fears God's limits, is accountable before God, and avoids corruption on earth. It does not oppress anyone on earth, because this authority has been granted to it on the basis that it is deemed worthy of it.

When there is complete separation between the people of truth and the people of falsehood, then against the lowly worldly power of the rebels and dictators, the great power of God appears as the Mighty, the Irresistible, the All-Encompassing. Because the mission of the messengers' preaching comes to an end, truth and falsehood stand arrayed against each other, and believers become distinguished from the liars. The situation then becomes this: on one side, in one camp, the power of the rebels of the world confronts them, while on the other side stand the messengers and the callers to truth, and with them is the great power of God. Both sides pray for victory and success, and the outcome unfolds accordingly.

This is a strange scene. In it, every rebellious dictator is brought to ruin. In this world's battlefield he is defeated, yet after this scene raises him up, another imagined scene is projected on the screen. Now he is inside Hell in the Hereafter, where he is extremely thirsty, and a liquid oozing from human wounds is being given to him to drink. He does not want to drink it, yet it is forced upon him. It does not go down his throat, because it is bitter and foul-tasting, a filthy and repulsive drink. The dictator's expression of disgust and pain is clearly visible in the words on the screen. The situation is that the torment coming at him from every side is so severe that he might seem about to die, but he is not even permitted to die. Torment upon torment is coming upon him, and that is precisely why he does not die.

This is a strange scene. In it, a defeated tyrant and dictator is portrayed, and this portrayal is shown against a background, just as imagination comes in the midst of a scene.

Verse 18

This scene, of ashes being scattered on a day of violent storm wind, is one that occurs regularly and is familiar to everyone. Here the Qur'an draws a conclusion from this scene: that something is lost in a tangible way, that its owner cannot prevent its being lost in this manner, and that no benefit can be drawn from such a lost thing. In this stormy scene the meaning is presented in embodied form, and this scene affects human consciousness very deeply. Had the loss of deeds been expressed in a purely mental and philosophical manner, it would never have had such an effect. Through this it becomes well fixed in the mind that these deeds have been utterly wasted.

This scene sweeps away the stock of the deeds of the disbelievers, those deeds which are not established on the firm foundation of faith, which are not bound with a strong rope to their true causes, and whose source and motive is not connection with Allah. Such deeds fly away just as ashes fly away in a violent wind, and such deeds can neither be firmly established nor be organized, because the essential thing is not the action itself but the impulse upon which the action appears, since action is a mechanical movement, like a machine moving. For it is necessary that behind the action there be a motivating force, and that the action have a definite purpose.

In this scene there is complete correspondence between a deep inner reality and an outward image, and this scene expresses the meaning in an extremely effective, suggestive and engaging style, and then the conclusion that emerges fits this meaning.

﴿Dhalika huwa al-dalal al-baeed﴾ (14:18) "That is the far-reaching straying." This conclusion is as dark as the darkness of the flying ashes is in complete harmony with it: the disbeliever appears lost in the dust cloud of his own deeds.

Then a further glimpse, which comes in the next verse, is also in harmony with this scene. In the context of the discourse it is indicated to the people of Quraysh that the fate of the deniers of earlier nations is not something far off awaiting you. If you do not become upright, Allah will wipe you out and bring another people onto the field.

The Commentary of Sayyid Qutb, Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation), on Surah 14, verses 19–20:

Verses 19 to 20

The theme now turns from the subject of faith and disbelief, and from the contest between the messengers and the jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance), to the scenes of the heavens and the earth. In the style of the Qur'an, such a turning of address is a natural matter, and in the human consciousness this shift also creates the sense that the Islamic system of life and the Qur'anic style are a faithful and divine style, because between the human nature (fitrah) and the soul of the universe an exchange of messages takes place through a particular language. Human nature is in complete harmony with the silent universe; the moment a person turns toward this universe, he begins to receive its effects and messages.

Those people who observe this universe and yet their nature does not draw from the signs and messages of the nature of the universe, they should know that the machine of their nature has broken down and the receiver of this machine has become defective; their inner senses have become impaired. In the same way that an eye becomes blind, ears become deaf, and the tongue becomes mute, the parts are present but do not function. Those individuals in whom the important parts of their nature have been damaged are, in any case, no longer fit to lead this world. All those people fall into this category whose thinking has been overcome by materialism, even though they call themselves scientists, and wrongly apply the title of intellectuals to themselves. This is because knowledge and wisdom do not suspend human nature, and do not sever man from the soul of the universe, but rather join him to it. It is precisely such people whom the Qur'an calls blind, mute and deaf, and if the leadership of human life is in the hands of the blind, it can never be set right.

In the creation of the heavens and the earth there are indications of great power and firm order. Truth is extremely firm; there is strength both in its meaning and in the pronunciation of the word "haqq" (truth). This truth appears solid like a rock, just as the ashes of falsehood, scattered by a stormy wind, appear; which are seen flying far across the deserts and then vanish.

In this atmosphere, a severe warning is given to the opponents of the Islamic movement.

{If He wills, He can take you away and bring a new creation} (14:19). "He may take you away and bring a new creation in your place." And the Being who can create the heavens and the earth is capable of bringing some other creation in place of humans, or of removing one nation from the leadership of the earth and bringing in another nation. The meanings of nations disappearing from the stage of existence in this way fully accord with the scene in which the deeds of the disbelievers are seen running like ashes in a windstorm and vanishing from sight.

{And that is not difficult for Allah} (14:20): "That is not at all difficult for Allah," and the creation of the heavens and the earth bears witness to this. Then, in human history, the way nations have continually perished, and the decline of one and the rise of another have come to light, this too bears witness to it. Just as a storm easily scatters ashes, this task is even easier for Allah. The truth is that the Qur'an is a marvel of inimitable beauty, in which scenes, images and meanings are in harmony, and whose speech is extremely well-proportioned in words, meanings and scenes.

Now we come before another horizon of artistic imagery, beautiful expression and well-proportioned style of presentation. Just a little while ago, our eyes were watching the destruction of tyrants and dictators. In this very world, every dictator was humiliated and remained so. As the scene was on the screen, an idea also appeared on the scene behind it, in which his gathering on the Day of Resurrection was shown, although he was still being humiliated in this world. Now before us the gathering of these dictators is seen in the place of assembly, and this scene is coming while continuing the series of scenes of the great story of humanity. This may be the final scene. But this scene is one of the most strange and interesting scenes of the Resurrection, full of emotions and movements, and in it there are full dialogues between the misguided, the influential people who misled, and Satan. Look at it in the words of the Qur'an:

**Verses 21–22**

This is the story of the Islamic call and of those who carried it, and the story of those who denied it and of the dictators. It has now passed from the stage of this world to the stage of the Hereafter, and it is a remarkably vivid scene.

﴿And they will all come forth before Allah﴾ (14:21). "And when they all emerge before Allah and are exposed." Here stand the rebellious dictators, and here stand their weak-willed followers, who chose the role of humiliation and weakness. Satan too stands on one side. On the other side stand those who believed in the messengers and did righteous deeds. All of them are now in the Day of Resurrection, in an open field. For Allah they were always manifest, but today they themselves feel in their own awareness and consciousness that they are naked and without veil, because on the plain of gathering there is no screen or cover. The field is full, the curtain rises, and the dialogue begins.

﴿Then those who were weak will say to those who were arrogant, "We were your followers, so can you avail us anything against the punishment of Allah?"﴾ (14:21). Weak people of feeble character remain weak. They are the ones who renounce the supreme human treasure that Allah has given to every human being: the treasure of freedom, freedom of opinion, freedom of religion, ideology and action. By their own choice they abandoned their freedom, accepted slavery, and became slaves of the rebellious and the dictators. They have become servants and slaves of other than Allah, and in place of the service of Allah they have adopted the service of human beings. Yet in Islam weakness is no acceptable excuse. Weakness is itself a crime. Allah does not permit anyone to become the slave of another. He calls human beings to a dignified life: honour Me, come under My protection. Allah has made every human being free and honoured, and He does not permit anyone to sell his freedom, or to surrender before any material power, however great that power may be. No power is given by Allah the right to keep other human beings as its slaves. In Islam the freedom and honour of every person is respected. The greatest material power in the world can only end the bond between a human being's life and body; it can inflict torment and pain, but it cannot seize a person's freedom. No dictator can rule over the human conscience, the human spirit and the human intellect. Neither can anyone imprison the intellect, the spirit and the conscience. A person himself renounces conscience, spirit, intellect and freedom, and then, humiliated, he enters the ranks of the oppressed.

No human being can compel the weakest of the weak, in matters of belief, ideas, thought or conduct, to submit to the rebellious and the dictators. No one can force even the weakest person to accept the religion of a rebellious dictator, because Allah, the Creator and Provider who is the guardian and responsible for all, exists. Only weak people, by their own pleasure, do this. They made themselves weak; their strength and the strength of a rebellious dictator are equal. In terms of rank, status, wealth and property, these oppressed people are equal to the dictator. The position and office of a dictator cannot make anyone weak. Rather, these are people of feeble character, weak in their faith and spirit, dishonoured and disgraced, who sell their freedom and honour for trivial gains, and who bow down, although honour, dignity and freedom are the most precious assets of a human being.

We see that these feeble people are a crowd, while the rebellious and the dictators are a few. Why does this crowd submit to the slavery of a few? In truth, these common people lack courage. They are spiritually defeated. There is no zeal within them, no self-respect, and they are inwardly and spiritually defeated before these dictators.

The reality is that a dictator humiliates the common masses only through their own consent. If the masses stand up, no dictator can remain standing before them. But this situation is due to the weak will of the masses themselves.

Humiliation descends upon a person only when he has the capacity to be humiliated. The dictator always takes advantage of the people's weakness. Now look at the mentality of the weak, and see how they behave on the Day of Resurrection. From their words it becomes clear that they were, and still are, people of very feeble character.

﴿Indeed, we were your followers in this world. Can you then avail us anything against the punishment of Allah?﴾ (14:21). This submission of yours has brought us to this end, which is a most tragic end. Or perhaps their purpose is only this: they have now seen the punishment of Allah, and now they wish to rebuke these arrogant leaders, saying that this is what your leadership and guidance have produced, so now go forward into this punishment. In any case, whatever their meaning, in every case it also points to their own humiliation, and it indicates the response of the deniers.

﴿They will say, "Had Allah guided us, we would have guided you. It is now the same for us whether we bear it impatiently or patiently; there is no escape for us."﴾ (14:21). This is a reluctant and decisive reply: "Had Allah shown us a path to salvation, we would certainly have shown it to you." Now why do you blame us? Our path is one and our end is one. When did we walk on the path of salvation so that we could have misled you? Had we been granted guidance, you too would have been on the path of guidance with us, just as our misguidance misled you. Now, on the Day of Resurrection, these people attribute their guidance and their error to Allah. Now they acknowledge the greatness of Allah and believe in Allah, although in the world they used to oppress the weak in such a way as if no one were there to call these rebellious ones to account, no mighty and dominant one. Now they wish to attribute guidance and misguidance to Allah in order to escape responsibility for them, although did Allah not command them not to go astray?

﴿Indeed, Allah does not command immorality﴾ (7:28). But beneath this, they also blame the weak by nature. Their meaning is that now there is no benefit in lamenting, and no benefit in patience. The punishment has been decided; by patience or by lamentation it will not be lifted. Now the door of repentance is closed. If it had been open, misguided people could have cried out and come to guidance. Had there been hardship in the world and you had been patient, there would still have been hope in Allah's mercy. Now the respite is over, and there is no way to escape the punishment.

﴿It is now the same for us whether we bear it impatiently or patiently; there is no escape for us﴾ (14:21). Here appears a surprising figure. Satan appears, the caller to misguidance and the singer of rebellion. He comes onto the stage in the robe of the pious, and appears like a soothsayer, and he displays his satanic pride before both parties, inflicting such a wound on them that this verbal wound may be bitterer than the punishment of Hell.

﴿And Satan will say, when the matter has been decided: "Indeed, Allah promised you a promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you. I had no authority over you. I only called you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I can neither help you, nor can you help me. I deny your association of me with Allah from before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers there is a painful punishment."﴾ (14:22). Indeed, Satan is Satan. In this scene he is in his complete form, just as the arrogant dictators and the oppressed people of feeble character are in their true form. God forbid.

This is the same Satan who used to whisper into hearts, deceive people into wickedness and sin, and make disbelief appealing to them. He used to prevent people from hearing the Islamic call. Today he addresses them with stinging, mocking and painful irony, saying that the fault is their own. Now they cannot even answer the truths he states, because what he says is the final judgement that has already been passed. He now speaks the truth, but too late.

﴿Indeed, Allah promised you a promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you﴾ (14:22). After this, Satan inflicts them with a new taunt, asking why they responded to his call, since he had no power over them. The only thing was that you people forgot your own selves, you overlooked the enmity between me and you, and you accepted my false call, and abandoned the true call of the prophets.

﴿I had no authority over you; I only called you, and you responded to me﴾ (14:22). After this he humiliates them further, saying: do not blame me; rather you yourselves deserve reproach for having obeyed me.

﴿So do not blame me; blame yourselves﴾ (14:22). Now he leaves them to their own condition and withdraws from them, although he himself had made promises to them, given them hopes, and planted doubts in their hearts that nothing would go wrong for them. Now, while they cry out, he gives them no help; and even if they cry out to him, they cannot help him in any way.

﴿I can neither help you, nor can you help me﴾ (14:22). Now there is no connection and no friendship between us.

Now he declares his disavowal, saying that you associated me with Allah. He plainly denies it, saying that he never said any such thing.

﴿I deny your association of me with Allah from before﴾ (14:22). Satan concludes his speech with a statement that is extremely discouraging to his friends.

﴿Indeed, for the wrongdoers there is a painful punishment﴾ (14:22). Look at the character of Satan! This is the very one who was calling them to misguidance, and they went astray at his word. The messengers of Allah were calling them to the path of the Messenger, and these people did not heed the messengers; they refused.

Before the curtain falls on this scene, from the other side a group of believers appears. These are the people who today have triumphed on the Day of Resurrection. The decision about their salvation has been made.
