Now he declares his disavowal, saying that you associated me with Allah. He plainly denies it, saying that he never said any such thing.

﴿I deny your association of me with Allah from before﴾ (14:22). Satan concludes his speech with a statement that is extremely discouraging to his friends.

﴿Indeed, for the wrongdoers there is a painful punishment﴾ (14:22). Look at the character of Satan! This is the very one who was calling them to misguidance, and they went astray at his word. The messengers of Allah were calling them to the path of the Messenger, and these people did not heed the messengers; they refused.

Before the curtain falls on this scene, from the other side a group of believers appears. These are the people who today have triumphed on the Day of Resurrection. The decision about their salvation has been made.

Verse 23

Now the curtain falls... What a beautiful scene it is. What a beautiful story this is of the Islamic call, its callers, its deniers, and the rebellious dictators.

Cast your eyes back once more over all the scenes of this story and keep its atmosphere in mind. In the first scene, the struggle between the Islamic movement and jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance and pre-Islamic unbelief) was shown on this earth. The group of the noble messengers stood against the rebellious.

"And they sought a judgment, and every obstinate tyrant was defeated. Behind him is Hell, where he will be given putrid water to drink, which he will sip but scarcely swallow, and death will come to him from every side, yet he will not die; and behind him there will be a severe punishment." (14:15-17)

Then, on the stage of the Hereafter too, we have just witnessed that extraordinary scene. It consisted of a strange dialogue between rebellious dictators, oppressive and arrogant people, and Satan himself. Now, after these scenes in the atmosphere of this excellent narrative, showing the good end of the righteous and the evil end of the wicked, Allah gives the example of good words and the correct worldview, and of bad words and corrupt philosophies, and explains that the struggle between the good and the bad, the pure and the impure, continues throughout a person's whole life. In other words, now that the story has ended and the curtain has fallen, this entire story is being commented upon.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (*Fi Zilal al-Quran*, Urdu translation) on Surah 14, verses 24–27 (part 1 of 2):

Verses 24 to 27

The good word is compared to a good tree that always bears fruit, is always flourishing, and the evil word is compared to worthless weeds, which the farmer uproots wherever he sees them, considering them useless and harmful. They have no place to settle. This parable and the scene it depicts are drawn from the stories of the prophets and of the rebellious tyrants and dictators. The parable is based on the outcome described in these stories, for the prophets and callers to truth, and for the rebellious deniers. The line of the prophets is a blessed tree whose root is Abraham (peace be upon him), the father of the prophets. In different seasons of history this tree has continued to bear its fruit. In every age some prophet has come, and it has continued to bear the fruit of reform, invitation and faith, through which the means of goodness and a good life have been provided.

But this parable, besides being in harmony with the atmosphere of this surah and the atmosphere of its story, has a very wide horizon of meanings, and deep realities lie within it. The good word means the word of truth, which is like a beneficial tree with firm roots. This truth is stable, solid and beneficial. Ages pass, but it remains in its place. The stormy winds of falsehood cannot shake it from its place, and the axes of oppression and rebellion cannot uproot it, although at times it appears that the harsh storms of oppression and rebellion will tear it out from the root. These trees are extremely tall, and their branches reach far into the skies. They look down with contempt from great heights upon rebellion and oppression. Although at times it seems that evil is contending with it even in the high skies, the fruit of this tree keeps coming, then the seed of this tree is sown in the hearts of righteous people, its saplings keep growing, and it keeps increasing generation after generation.

The evil word, which is falsehood, is like a worthless bush and weed. Sometimes these bushes also show a spring and take the form of dense forests, and some people are influenced by them. They think that perhaps the tree of falsehood has outgrown the truth. But it has no roots. It is uprooted with little effort, just as weeds are pulled out from a crop. People uproot it before their eyes, and therefore it is deprived of settlement and endurance, because it is by nature evil.

This is not merely a parable or a proverb, nor is it a statement by which good people are being encouraged. Rather, this parable is a reality of life. Although at times there is a delay in this reality becoming manifest, the fact is that truth and goodness can never be uprooted from their foundation, and this truth never dies or is annihilated, even though evil may have a firm grip and may block its path. Similarly, pure evil also does not flourish in the world. In reality, it mixes in some portion of good, and when the elements of good mixed with that evil are exhausted, then evil dies its own death. Although apparently it appears to have great power and immense strength, the true reality is that good always prevails in the end, and evil always faces difficulties.

﴿Thus does Allah set forth parables for people, that they may take heed﴾ (14:25). These are parables that exist on earth in the form of reality. People do not reflect upon them. The Qur'an only draws people's attention, because it is a reminder.

In the metaphor of the firm tree, there is also a depiction of the steadfastness of truth, in that the roots of truth are deep and it has branches reaching the sky, and it is evident that it is high. Truth stands firm, and it demonstrates that it is strong and solid. What does Allah intend by giving this parable through this good word and good tree?

﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word, in this world and in the Hereafter﴾ (14:27). By giving the parable of the evil word, which is like an evil tree, having no stability or settlement for it,

﴿And Allah leads the wrongdoers astray﴾ (14:27). Thus there is complete harmony between the style of speech and the meaning intended. Allah grants stability and firmness to the people of faith in this life, their word is made firm here, and in the Hereafter He strengthens them, and there their end is firm, because faith stands firmly in the soil of their hearts. It becomes part of their nature, and righteous deeds keep flowing from this tree into their lives. These deeds come one after another. This tree grows stronger and stronger through the teachings of the Qur'an and Sunnah. Before it stands a lamp of hope, and there is certainty of success in this world and the Hereafter. All these matters, or fruits, are true and solid. There is one path and one method. In the land of the hearts of those in whom this tree stands, there is no anguish, restlessness, bewilderment or agitation.

Because of their oppression and polytheism (in the Qur'an, oppression generally refers to polytheism), the wrongdoers are kept away from light and illumination. These people wander in the narrow and dark valleys of superstitions and myths. They walk on various paths of desire. Deprived of the one path of Allah, Allah, according to His continuing practice, then further misguides them, because they themselves adopted the path of oppression, darkness and the worship of desire. So they wandered and ran about in the paths of evil.

﴿And Allah does what He wills﴾ (14:27). His will is unrestricted. It is true that He establishes a natural law, but He Himself is not bound by His natural law. However, He approves of those who follow His law. If He wills, He also changes the natural law that He has established, because there is no power that can restrain Allah. He acts as He wills, and what He wills happens.

With this commentary, the great account of the noble messengers and the matter of their story come to an end. This was the story of the call of Islam. Its first part spread over a large portion at the beginning of this surah. Here was the story of Abraham, the father of the prophets. Then there was the story of several other prophets, whose branches spread far across history, and they were the gardeners of the tree of the good word, which flourished like truth. The good word that all these prophets brought was like the blessed tree. It was the word of Tawhid (monotheism). The blessed tree of all the prophets was one; it bore one fruit. This word was Tawhid, and in all the prophets this word remained one, and the call also remained one.

This was the long conflict between Islam and jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam). We have made brief allusions to it throughout this surah. I consider it necessary to reflect again somewhat upon these allusions.

From this story it becomes clear that throughout human history the caravan of faith is one caravan. From Adam (peace be upon him) onward this caravan has been moving, and the messengers are its leaders. The call of all the prophets was towards one ideology and belief. They raised one voice and worked on one method. The call of all of them was that the one God and ruler is one, He alone is Lord, and there is no other god, lord or ruler besides Him. The people of faith should place their trust in none but Him, should not seek refuge in anyone other than Allah, and should not regard anyone other than Allah as their support.

So let one who understands that Allah is one, and the history of the belief in Tawhid, which nowadays the scholars of "comparative religion" (*taqabul adyan*) go around describing, consider that people first believed in many gods, then began to believe in two gods, namely "gods of good and evil". In this way, people first worshipped trees and stones, the sun, moon, stars and planets, and then in the end they began to worship the one God. Thus their views evolved, and human knowledge and philosophy kept progressing. In the same way, their society also progressed, to the point of the establishment of the kingship of a king.

But the real fact is that since the beginning of human history, all the messengers have preached the belief in Tawhid. The fundamental element in the mission and call of all the messengers was this, and there is no exception to it. Among all the well-known heavenly religions, according to the Qur'an, their call was this.

If the scholars of comparative religion were to put their case in this way: that the belief in Tawhid which the messengers expressed from Adam (peace be upon him) up to Muhammad (ﷺ), afterwards, for the understanding of human beings, there was an evolution in human comprehension, such that through the continuous struggle of the noble messengers this light spread gradually among the common people, and in the end more people became ready to accept the religion of Allah, the belief in Tawhid, after this long struggle, then the view of these scholars of comparative religion would appear reasonable. But the reality is that these people are influenced by the research methodology that is prevalent in Europe. Beneath this methodology, in fact, lies hidden enmity against the Church, and it is regrettable that modern Muslim thinkers too have not kept this in mind. In any case, comparative religion, knowingly or unknowingly, runs against the correct Islamic and religious way of thinking, and this approach demonstrates that religions are not based on revelation, but that religion too is in reality an evolution of human thought. Just as other human ideas, philosophies and experiments have evolved, so too has religious thought continued to evolve. In short, it is the result of this ancient hostility and this way of thinking that the experts of comparative religion in our age speak in this manner, and they call their thinking and view scholarly and research-based.

If a person of another country or nation is deceived by this methodology, let him be deceived, but a Muslim cannot be influenced by this methodology even for a single minute. Muslims have a correct methodology of thought regarding their religion, and they have certain settled principles of their own regarding religion, and they have their own method of discussion.

In short, all the prophets presented one call to humanity. They gave one ideology. And in accordance with this same methodology, in their respective ages, they confronted jahiliyyah. The Qur'an clearly states that all the messengers came with this call, presenting this one ideology, and in every age they confronted jahiliyyah in one and the same way. And in this matter the Qur'an has given no indication of any evolution with regard to time and place.

This is a reality that invites us to reflection: that Islam is Islam and jahiliyyah is jahiliyyah. Islam has always remained Islam, and jahiliyyah has always remained jahiliyyah. In no period of history has there been any unity between them. Whenever a society has been built on the basis of Islam, it has had one and the same character, and whenever any gathering has taken place on the basis of jahiliyyah, it too has remained of one kind. For example, the first characteristic of jahiliyyah is that in it a human being is the slave of another human being, and in it the ruler is not Allah but someone else. The one who nurtures is also someone else. Whether one believes in many gods, or believes in one God but the lords and rulers are many, this society will still be a jahili society, and all the features and marks of jahiliyyah will be present in this society.

The foundation of the call of the messengers has been that Allah should be regarded as one, and all false gods should be rejected. Religion should belong to Allah alone, obedience should be to the religion and law of Allah alone, and Allah alone should be regarded as the ruler and lawgiver. This view is directly the opposite of the view that has been the foundation of jahiliyyah. As soon as anyone declares that the ruler too shall be Allah, and the law too shall be the law of Allah, every jahiliyyah regards him as a threat to itself, especially when people gather around this view and adopt a collective life, and especially when these individuals are breaking away from jahiliyyah and forming a gathering, in such a situation the jahili ideology and the jahili ruler regard the gathering of such individuals as a rebellion against themselves. Then every jahili government thinks that the belief of these people is suspect. Yet these matters are such that in every age it is essential for the Islamic movement to openly proclaim its ideas, then to form an organization on their basis, and then for these people to work together. In every age this method is necessary.

In every age the system of jahiliyyah has a system, and it has an organic structure. When it sees that an opposing ideological system has come against it, and a new society is also being formed which has a completely opposite organic structure and system to its own society, because beneath the jahili society lies the idea of many gods, in it there are many rulers, and in it human beings are slaves and followers of human beings, while in the Islamic society there is the idea of one God and ruler, and in it all people are servants of Allah. No one is the servant of another. Then the jahili society regards this new society as a threat to itself.

The threat increases further from the fact that this newly formed Islamic society gradually consumes the body of the jahili society. At the beginning, when the Islamic society is formed, the threat is small, but when it makes the demand upon jahiliyyah that people should be freed from their slavery, and that all of you should enter into the slavery of Allah, then, since this has been the method of the messengers from the beginning, the call of Islam and the Islamic movement, from the very beginning, in every age, jahiliyyah has regarded the Islamic movement as a challenge to its own existence. This matter is well understood and appears natural. It is like an established entity defending itself against an attacker, and like every person who has seized sovereignty from the people struggling with hands and feet to preserve his power.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (*Fi Zilal al-Quran*, Urdu translation) on Surah 14, verses 24–27 (part 2 of 2):

When *jahiliyyah* (the state of ignorance of divine guidance) perceives that the Islamic movement has become a threat to its existence, it too has regarded this confrontation as a matter of life and death. *Jahiliyyah* has never adopted the principles of gentleness, compromise, peace and safety with the Islamic movement. *Jahiliyyah* has never deceived itself in this struggle. Nor have the noble messengers ever deceived themselves in this struggle, and nor has any believing *da'i* (caller to Islam) after them deceived himself in this regard. This has been the declaration of *jahiliyyah*:

﴿وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِرُسُلِهِمْ لَنُخْرِجَنَّكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِنَا أَوْ لَتَعُودُنَّ فِي مِلَّتِنَا﴾ (14:13) "And those who disbelieved said to their messengers: 'We will surely expel you from our land, or you must return to our community.'" These people were not prepared to accept that the messengers and the believers had a separate existence, that they might have their own ideology or their own party. Their demand is: come back to our party, or be ready to be exiled. Come back, do not stand apart; merge into our society, dissolve, and do not form your own separate society and collectivity.

But the noble messengers also never accepted that they should dissolve and merge into *millat al-jahiliyyah* (the community of ignorance), destroy their existence and erase their identity. This is because their society is founded on an entirely new ideology, a new constitution and a new charter, which stands in contradiction to the ideology, constitution and charter of *jahiliyyah*. The messengers neither gave such a response nor acted in such a manner as some ignorant people of our age say: merge into the *jahili* society, work from within, and spread your creed inside it.

The reality is that when the people of *da'wah* rise in a *jahili* society with a new Islamic ideology, then on the basis of that ideology their society, their leadership and their loyalties automatically separate. This is a natural matter; no one's intention plays a part in it. This natural and necessary process is inherent in the formation of any society. If, as a result of this process, a reaction arises within a *jahili* society because people are being gathered upon the worship, sovereignty, law, constitution and charter of One God alone, then this reaction too is natural. All the cogs of that *jahili* system then work again against Islam. If any Muslim becomes a cog in that *jahili* society, then in reality he will be a servant of that *jahili* society, not of Islam, just as some fools think: become a cog of *jahiliyyah* and serve Islam.

After this comes the reality that is destined for every *da'wah*, and for everyone who carries out the work of the Islamic *da'wah* in any time or place. It is this: Allah has promised His friends help, and He has surely said that My help will come and they will be given authority on earth. This promise will not take the form of reality until they are distinguished from a *jahili* society and separate from it, and until, on the basis of this *da'wah*, they separate from their people and form their own society and their own community. If they remain a part of a *jahili* society, moving about within it and being its cogs, then even though they hold the Islamic way of life as their belief and work for it, the fulfilment of Allah's help and promise will be delayed. This is the indispensable, great and fundamental condition, which those who carry out the work of Islamic *da'wah* must fully fulfil. They must understand this well.

Finally, there is another aspect worthy of reflection: how beautifully the Qur'an presents this caravan of the noble messengers. This caravan has been confronting *jahiliyyah* throughout human history with remarkable beauty and steadfastness. This portrayal is beautiful because the truth carried by the travellers of this caravan is extremely simple, natural and beautiful. These travellers are content, serious, and walking on their path with ....

﴿قَالَتْ لَهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ إِن نَّحْنُ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَمُنُّ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ﴾ ... ﴿فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ (14:11) "Their messengers said to them: 'Indeed, we are nothing but humans like you, but Allah bestows His favour upon whom He wills among His servants.' And it is not for us to bring you any authority, except by Allah's leave; and upon Allah let the believers rely."

This dazzling beauty arises because this is a single, unified caravan which, in every time and place, has confronted a unified *jahiliyyah*, in every age and in every nation.

Then this beauty appears to us from another angle as well: the deep connection between this *da'wah* and the truth carried by these noble messengers, and the truth hidden in this universe, because the messengers say:

﴿أَفِي اللَّهِ شَكٌّ فَاطِرِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ (14:10) "Is there doubt about Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth?" And in another verse:

﴿وَمَا لَنَا أَلَّا نَتَوَكَّلَ عَلَى اللَّهِ وَقَدْ هَدَانَا سُبُلَنَا﴾ (14:12) "And why should we not rely upon Allah, when He has guided us in our ways?" And elsewhere:

﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ ۚ إِن يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ وَيَأْتِ بِخَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ * وَمَا ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ بِعَزِيزٍ﴾ (14:19–20) "Do you not see that Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth? If He wills, He can remove you and bring a new creation. And that is not difficult for Allah."

Thus a deep connection is established between this cosmic truth and the truth of the Islamic *da'wah*, and from this it becomes clear that the Divine Being, who is the Truth, is the source of both these truths, and that these truths are deeply established, firm, and have roots reaching far into this universe.

﴿وَمَثَلُ كَلِمَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ كَشَجَرَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ ... مَا لَهَا مِن قَرَارٍ﴾ (14:26) "And the likeness of an evil word is that of an evil tree, uprooted from the earth's surface; it has no stability."

If a person of another country or nation is deceived by this methodology, let him be deceived, but a Muslim cannot be influenced by this methodology even for a single minute. Muslims have a correct methodology of thought regarding their religion, and they have certain settled principles of their own regarding religion, and they have their own method of discussion.

In short, all the prophets presented one call to humanity. They gave one ideology. And in accordance with this same methodology, in their respective ages, they confronted jahiliyyah. The Qur'an clearly states that all the messengers came with this call, presenting this one ideology, and in every age they confronted jahiliyyah in one and the same way. And in this matter the Qur'an has given no indication of any evolution with regard to time and place.

This is a reality that invites us to reflection: that Islam is Islam and jahiliyyah is jahiliyyah. Islam has always remained Islam, and jahiliyyah has always remained jahiliyyah. In no period of history has there been any unity between them. Whenever a society has been built on the basis of Islam, it has had one and the same character, and whenever any gathering has taken place on the basis of jahiliyyah, it too has remained of one kind. For example, the first characteristic of jahiliyyah is that in it a human being is the slave of another human being, and in it the ruler is not Allah but someone else. The one who nurtures is also someone else. Whether one believes in many gods, or believes in one God but the lords and rulers are many, this society will still be a jahili society, and all the features and marks of jahiliyyah will be present in this society.

The foundation of the call of the messengers has been that Allah should be regarded as one, and all false gods should be rejected. Religion should belong to Allah alone, obedience should be to the religion and law of Allah alone, and Allah alone should be regarded as the ruler and lawgiver. This view is directly the opposite of the view that has been the foundation of jahiliyyah. As soon as anyone declares that the ruler too shall be Allah, and the law too shall be the law of Allah, every jahiliyyah regards him as a threat to itself, especially when people gather around this view and adopt a collective life, and especially when these individuals are breaking away from jahiliyyah and forming a gathering, in such a situation the jahili ideology and the jahili ruler regard the gathering of such individuals as a rebellion against themselves. Then every jahili government thinks that the belief of these people is suspect. Yet these matters are such that in every age it is essential for the Islamic movement to openly proclaim its ideas, then to form an organization on their basis, and then for these people to work together. In every age this method is necessary.

In every age the system of jahiliyyah has a system, and it has an organic structure. When it sees that an opposing ideological system has come against it, and a new society is also being formed which has a completely opposite organic structure and system to its own society, because beneath the jahili society lies the idea of many gods, in it there are many rulers, and in it human beings are slaves and followers of human beings, while in the Islamic society there is the idea of one God and ruler, and in it all people are servants of Allah. No one is the servant of another. Then the jahili society regards this new society as a threat to itself.

The threat increases further from the fact that this newly formed Islamic society gradually consumes the body of the jahili society. At the beginning, when the Islamic society is formed, the threat is small, but when it makes the demand upon jahiliyyah that people should be freed from their slavery, and that all of you should enter into the slavery of Allah, then, since this has been the method of the messengers from the beginning, the call of Islam and the Islamic movement, from the very beginning, in every age, jahiliyyah has regarded the Islamic movement as a challenge to its own existence. This matter is well understood and appears natural. It is like an established entity defending itself against an attacker, and like every person who has seized sovereignty from the people struggling with hands and feet to preserve his power.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (*Fi Zilal al-Quran*, Urdu translation) on Surah 14, verses 24–27 (part 2 of 2):

When *jahiliyyah* (the state of ignorance of divine guidance) perceives that the Islamic movement has become a threat to its existence, it too has regarded this confrontation as a matter of life and death. *Jahiliyyah* has never adopted the principles of gentleness, compromise, peace and safety with the Islamic movement. *Jahiliyyah* has never deceived itself in this struggle. Nor have the noble messengers ever deceived themselves in this struggle, and nor has any believing *da'i* (caller to Islam) after them deceived himself in this regard. This has been the declaration of *jahiliyyah*:

﴿وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِرُسُلِهِمْ لَنُخْرِجَنَّكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِنَا أَوْ لَتَعُودُنَّ فِي مِلَّتِنَا﴾ (14:13) "And those who disbelieved said to their messengers: 'We will surely expel you from our land, or you must return to our community.'" These people were not prepared to accept that the messengers and the believers had a separate existence, that they might have their own ideology or their own party. Their demand is: come back to our party, or be ready to be exiled. Come back, do not stand apart; merge into our society, dissolve, and do not form your own separate society and collectivity.

But the noble messengers also never accepted that they should dissolve and merge into *millat al-jahiliyyah* (the community of ignorance), destroy their existence and erase their identity. This is because their society is founded on an entirely new ideology, a new constitution and a new charter, which stands in contradiction to the ideology, constitution and charter of *jahiliyyah*. The messengers neither gave such a response nor acted in such a manner as some ignorant people of our age say: merge into the *jahili* society, work from within, and spread your creed inside it.

The reality is that when the people of *da'wah* rise in a *jahili* society with a new Islamic ideology, then on the basis of that ideology their society, their leadership and their loyalties automatically separate. This is a natural matter; no one's intention plays a part in it. This natural and necessary process is inherent in the formation of any society. If, as a result of this process, a reaction arises within a *jahili* society because people are being gathered upon the worship, sovereignty, law, constitution and charter of One God alone, then this reaction too is natural. All the cogs of that *jahili* system then work again against Islam. If any Muslim becomes a cog in that *jahili* society, then in reality he will be a servant of that *jahili* society, not of Islam, just as some fools think: become a cog of *jahiliyyah* and serve Islam.

After this comes the reality that is destined for every *da'wah*, and for everyone who carries out the work of the Islamic *da'wah* in any time or place. This promise will not take the form of reality until they are distinguished from a *jahili* society and separate from it, and until, on the basis of this *da'wah*, they separate from their people and form their own society and their own community. They have no place to settle. This parable and the scene it depicts are drawn from the stories of the prophets and of the rebellious tyrants and dictators. The parable is based on the outcome described in these stories, for the prophets and callers to truth, and for the rebellious deniers. The line of the prophets is a blessed tree whose root is Abraham (peace be upon him), the father of the prophets. In different seasons of history this tree has continued to bear its fruit. In every age some prophet has come, and it has continued to bear the fruit of reform, invitation and faith, through which the means of goodness and a good life have been provided.

But this parable, besides being in harmony with the atmosphere of this surah and the atmosphere of its story, has a very wide horizon of meanings, and deep realities lie within it. The good word means the word of truth, which is like a beneficial tree with firm roots. This truth is stable, solid and beneficial. Ages pass, but it remains in its place. The stormy winds of falsehood cannot shake it from its place, and the axes of oppression and rebellion cannot uproot it, although at times it appears that the harsh storms of oppression and rebellion will tear it out from the root. These trees are extremely tall, and their branches reach far into the skies. They look down with contempt from great heights upon rebellion and oppression. Although at times it seems that evil is contending with it even in the high skies, the fruit of this tree keeps coming, then the seed of this tree is sown in the hearts of righteous people, its saplings keep growing, and it keeps increasing generation after generation.

The evil word, which is falsehood, is like a worthless bush and weed. Sometimes these bushes also show a spring and take the form of dense forests, and some people are influenced by them. They think that perhaps the tree of falsehood has outgrown the truth. But it has no roots. It is uprooted with little effort, just as weeds are pulled out from a crop. People uproot it before their eyes, and therefore it is deprived of settlement and endurance, because it is by nature evil.

This is not merely a parable or a proverb, nor is it a statement by which good people are being encouraged. Rather, this parable is a reality of life. Although at times there is a delay in this reality becoming manifest, the fact is that truth and goodness can never be uprooted from their foundation, and this truth never dies or is annihilated, even though evil may have a firm grip and may block its path. Similarly, pure evil also does not flourish in the world. In reality, it mixes in some portion of good, and when the elements of good mixed with that evil are exhausted, then evil dies its own death. Although apparently it appears to have great power and immense strength, the true reality is that good always prevails in the end, and evil always faces difficulties.

﴿Thus does Allah set forth parables for people, that they may take heed﴾ (14:25). These are parables that exist on earth in the form of reality. People do not reflect upon them. The Qur'an only draws people's attention, because it is a reminder.

Truth stands firm, and it demonstrates that it is strong and solid. What does Allah intend by giving this parable through this good word and good tree?

﴿And Allah leads the wrongdoers astray﴾ (14:27). Thus there is complete harmony between the style of speech and the meaning intended. Allah grants stability and firmness to the people of faith in this life, their word is made firm here, and in the Hereafter He strengthens them, and there their end is firm, because faith stands firmly in the soil of their hearts. It becomes part of their nature, and righteous deeds keep flowing from this tree into their lives. These deeds come one after another. This tree grows stronger and stronger through the teachings of the Qur'an and Sunnah. Before it stands a lamp of hope, and there is certainty of success in this world and the Hereafter. All these matters, or fruits, are true and solid. There is one path and one method. In the land of the hearts of those in whom this tree stands, there is no anguish, restlessness, bewilderment or agitation.

Because of their oppression and polytheism (in the Qur'an, oppression generally refers to polytheism), the wrongdoers are kept away from light and illumination. These people wander in the narrow and dark valleys of superstitions and myths. They walk on various paths of desire. Deprived of the one path of Allah, Allah, according to His continuing practice, then further misguides them, because they themselves adopted the path of oppression, darkness and the worship of desire. So they wandered and ran about in the paths of evil.

He acts as He wills, and what He wills happens.

Thus a deep connection is established between this cosmic truth and the truth of the Islamic *da'wah*, and from this it becomes clear that the Divine Being, who is the Truth, is the source of both these truths, and that these truths are deeply established, firm, and have roots reaching far into this universe.

﴿وَمَثَلُ كَلِمَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ كَشَجَرَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ ... مَا لَهَا مِن قَرَارٍ﴾ (14:26) "And the likeness of an evil word is that of an evil tree, uprooted from the earth's surface; it has no stability."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (*Fi Zilal al-Quran*, Urdu translation) on Surah 14, verses 24–27 (part 1 of 2):

Verses 24 to 27

The good word is compared to a good tree that always bears fruit, is always flourishing, and the evil word is compared to worthless weeds, which the farmer uproots wherever he sees them, considering them useless and harmful. They have no place to settle. This parable and the scene it depicts are drawn from the stories of the prophets and of the rebellious tyrants and dictators. The parable is based on the outcome described in these stories, for the prophets and callers to truth, and for the rebellious deniers. The line of the prophets is a blessed tree whose root is Abraham (peace be upon him), the father of the prophets. In different seasons of history this tree has continued to bear its fruit. In every age some prophet has come, and it has continued to bear the fruit of reform, invitation and faith, through which the means of goodness and a good life have been provided.

But this parable, besides being in harmony with the atmosphere of this surah and the atmosphere of its story, has a very wide horizon of meanings, and deep realities lie within it. The good word means the word of truth, which is like a beneficial tree with firm roots. This truth is stable, solid and beneficial. Ages pass, but it remains in its place. The stormy winds of falsehood cannot shake it from its place, and the axes of oppression and rebellion cannot uproot it, although at times it appears that the harsh storms of oppression and rebellion will tear it out from the root. These trees are extremely tall, and their branches reach far into the skies. They look down with contempt from great heights upon rebellion and oppression. Although at times it seems that evil is contending with it even in the high skies, the fruit of this tree keeps coming, then the seed of this tree is sown in the hearts of righteous people, its saplings keep growing, and it keeps increasing generation after generation.

The evil word, which is falsehood, is like a worthless bush and weed. Sometimes these bushes also show a spring and take the form of dense forests, and some people are influenced by them. They think that perhaps the tree of falsehood has outgrown the truth. But it has no roots. It is uprooted with little effort, just as weeds are pulled out from a crop. People uproot it before their eyes, and therefore it is deprived of settlement and endurance, because it is by nature evil.

This is not merely a parable or a proverb, nor is it a statement by which good people are being encouraged. Rather, this parable is a reality of life. Although at times there is a delay in this reality becoming manifest, the fact is that truth and goodness can never be uprooted from their foundation, and this truth never dies or is annihilated, even though evil may have a firm grip and may block its path. Similarly, pure evil also does not flourish in the world. In reality, it mixes in some portion of good, and when the elements of good mixed with that evil are exhausted, then evil dies its own death. Although apparently it appears to have great power and immense strength, the true reality is that good always prevails in the end, and evil always faces difficulties.

﴿Thus does Allah set forth parables for people, that they may take heed﴾ (14:25). These are parables that exist on earth in the form of reality. People do not reflect upon them. The Qur'an only draws people's attention, because it is a reminder.

In the metaphor of the firm tree, there is also a depiction of the steadfastness of truth, in that the roots of truth are deep and it has branches reaching the sky, and it is evident that it is high. Truth stands firm, and it demonstrates that it is strong and solid. What does Allah intend by giving this parable through this good word and good tree?

﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word, in this world and in the Hereafter﴾ (14:27). By giving the parable of the evil word, which is like an evil tree, having no stability or settlement for it,

﴿And Allah leads the wrongdoers astray﴾ (14:27). Thus there is complete harmony between the style of speech and the meaning intended. Allah grants stability and firmness to the people of faith in this life, their word is made firm here, and in the Hereafter He strengthens them, and there their end is firm, because faith stands firmly in the soil of their hearts. It becomes part of their nature, and righteous deeds keep flowing from this tree into their lives. These deeds come one after another. This tree grows stronger and stronger through the teachings of the Qur'an and Sunnah. Before it stands a lamp of hope, and there is certainty of success in this world and the Hereafter. All these matters, or fruits, are true and solid. There is one path and one method. In the land of the hearts of those in whom this tree stands, there is no anguish, restlessness, bewilderment or agitation.

Because of their oppression and polytheism (in the Qur'an, oppression generally refers to polytheism), the wrongdoers are kept away from light and illumination. These people wander in the narrow and dark valleys of superstitions and myths. They walk on various paths of desire. Deprived of the one path of Allah, Allah, according to His continuing practice, then further misguides them, because they themselves adopted the path of oppression, darkness and the worship of desire. So they wandered and ran about in the paths of evil.

﴿And Allah does what He wills﴾ (14:27). His will is unrestricted. It is true that He establishes a natural law, but He Himself is not bound by His natural law. However, He approves of those who follow His law. If He wills, He also changes the natural law that He has established, because there is no power that can restrain Allah. He acts as He wills, and what He wills happens.

With this commentary, the great account of the noble messengers and the matter of their story come to an end. This was the story of the call of Islam. Its first part spread over a large portion at the beginning of this surah. Here was the story of Abraham, the father of the prophets. Then there was the story of several other prophets, whose branches spread far across history, and they were the gardeners of the tree of the good word, which flourished like truth. The good word that all these prophets brought was like the blessed tree. It was the word of Tawhid (monotheism). The blessed tree of all the prophets was one; it bore one fruit. This word was Tawhid, and in all the prophets this word remained one, and the call also remained one.

This was the long conflict between Islam and jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam). We have made brief allusions to it throughout this surah. I consider it necessary to reflect again somewhat upon these allusions.

From this story it becomes clear that throughout human history the caravan of faith is one caravan. From Adam (peace be upon him) onward this caravan has been moving, and the messengers are its leaders. The call of all the prophets was towards one ideology and belief. They raised one voice and worked on one method. The call of all of them was that the one God and ruler is one, He alone is Lord, and there is no other god, lord or ruler besides Him. The people of faith should place their trust in none but Him, should not seek refuge in anyone other than Allah, and should not regard anyone other than Allah as their support.

So let one who understands that Allah is one, and the history of the belief in Tawhid, which nowadays the scholars of "comparative religion" (*taqabul adyan*) go around describing, consider that people first believed in many gods, then began to believe in two gods, namely "gods of good and evil". In this way, people first worshipped trees and stones, the sun, moon, stars and planets, and then in the end they began to worship the one God. Thus their views evolved, and human knowledge and philosophy kept progressing. In the same way, their society also progressed, to the point of the establishment of the kingship of a king.

But the real fact is that since the beginning of human history, all the messengers have preached the belief in Tawhid. The fundamental element in the mission and call of all the messengers was this, and there is no exception to it. Among all the well-known heavenly religions, according to the Qur'an, their call was this.

If the scholars of comparative religion were to put their case in this way: that the belief in Tawhid which the messengers expressed from Adam (peace be upon him) up to Muhammad (ﷺ), afterwards, for the understanding of human beings, there was an evolution in human comprehension, such that through the continuous struggle of the noble messengers this light spread gradually among the common people, and in the end more people became ready to accept the religion of Allah, the belief in Tawhid, after this long struggle, then the view of these scholars of comparative religion would appear reasonable. But the reality is that these people are influenced by the research methodology that is prevalent in Europe. Beneath this methodology, in fact, lies hidden enmity against the Church, and it is regrettable that modern Muslim thinkers too have not kept this in mind. In any case, comparative religion, knowingly or unknowingly, runs against the correct Islamic and religious way of thinking, and this approach demonstrates that religions are not based on revelation, but that religion too is in reality an evolution of human thought. Just as other human ideas, philosophies and experiments have evolved, so too has religious thought continued to evolve. In short, it is the result of this ancient hostility and this way of thinking that the experts of comparative religion in our age speak in this manner, and they call their thinking and view scholarly and research-based.

If a person of another country or nation is deceived by this methodology, let him be deceived, but a Muslim cannot be influenced by this methodology even for a single minute. Muslims have a correct methodology of thought regarding their religion, and they have certain settled principles of their own regarding religion, and they have their own method of discussion.

In short, all the prophets presented one call to humanity. They gave one ideology. And in accordance with this same methodology, in their respective ages, they confronted jahiliyyah. The Qur'an clearly states that all the messengers came with this call, presenting this one ideology, and in every age they confronted jahiliyyah in one and the same way. And in this matter the Qur'an has given no indication of any evolution with regard to time and place.

This is a reality that invites us to reflection: that Islam is Islam and jahiliyyah is jahiliyyah. Islam has always remained Islam, and jahiliyyah has always remained jahiliyyah. In no period of history has there been any unity between them. Whenever a society has been built on the basis of Islam, it has had one and the same character, and whenever any gathering has taken place on the basis of jahiliyyah, it too has remained of one kind. For example, the first characteristic of jahiliyyah is that in it a human being is the slave of another human being, and in it the ruler is not Allah but someone else. The one who nurtures is also someone else. Whether one believes in many gods, or believes in one God but the lords and rulers are many, this society will still be a jahili society, and all the features and marks of jahiliyyah will be present in this society.

The foundation of the call of the messengers has been that Allah should be regarded as one, and all false gods should be rejected. Religion should belong to Allah alone, obedience should be to the religion and law of Allah alone, and Allah alone should be regarded as the ruler and lawgiver. This view is directly the opposite of the view that has been the foundation of jahiliyyah. As soon as anyone declares that the ruler too shall be Allah, and the law too shall be the law of Allah, every jahiliyyah regards him as a threat to itself, especially when people gather around this view and adopt a collective life, and especially when these individuals are breaking away from jahiliyyah and forming a gathering, in such a situation the jahili ideology and the jahili ruler regard the gathering of such individuals as a rebellion against themselves. Then every jahili government thinks that the belief of these people is suspect. Yet these matters are such that in every age it is essential for the Islamic movement to openly proclaim its ideas, then to form an organization on their basis, and then for these people to work together. In every age this method is necessary.

In every age the system of jahiliyyah has a system, and it has an organic structure. When it sees that an opposing ideological system has come against it, and a new society is also being formed which has a completely opposite organic structure and system to its own society, because beneath the jahili society lies the idea of many gods, in it there are many rulers, and in it human beings are slaves and followers of human beings, while in the Islamic society there is the idea of one God and ruler, and in it all people are servants of Allah. No one is the servant of another. Then the jahili society regards this new society as a threat to itself.

The threat increases further from the fact that this newly formed Islamic society gradually consumes the body of the jahili society. At the beginning, when the Islamic society is formed, the threat is small, but when it makes the demand upon jahiliyyah that people should be freed from their slavery, and that all of you should enter into the slavery of Allah, then, since this has been the method of the messengers from the beginning, the call of Islam and the Islamic movement, from the very beginning, in every age, jahiliyyah has regarded the Islamic movement as a challenge to its own existence. This matter is well understood and appears natural. It is like an established entity defending itself against an attacker, and like every person who has seized sovereignty from the people struggling with hands and feet to preserve his power.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (*Fi Zilal al-Quran*, Urdu translation) on Surah 14, verses 24–27 (part 2 of 2):

When *jahiliyyah* (the state of ignorance of divine guidance) perceives that the Islamic movement has become a threat to its existence, it too has regarded this confrontation as a matter of life and death. *Jahiliyyah* has never adopted the principles of gentleness, compromise, peace and safety with the Islamic movement. *Jahiliyyah* has never deceived itself in this struggle. Nor have the noble messengers ever deceived themselves in this struggle, and nor has any believing *da'i* (caller to Islam) after them deceived himself in this regard. This has been the declaration of *jahiliyyah*:

﴿وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِرُسُلِهِمْ لَنُخْرِجَنَّكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِنَا أَوْ لَتَعُودُنَّ فِي مِلَّتِنَا﴾ (14:13) "And those who disbelieved said to their messengers: 'We will surely expel you from our land, or you must return to our community.'" These people were not prepared to accept that the messengers and the believers had a separate existence, that they might have their own ideology or their own party. Their demand is: come back to our party, or be ready to be exiled. Come back, do not stand apart; merge into our society, dissolve, and do not form your own separate society and collectivity.

But the noble messengers also never accepted that they should dissolve and merge into *millat al-jahiliyyah* (the community of ignorance), destroy their existence and erase their identity. This is because their society is founded on an entirely new ideology, a new constitution and a new charter, which stands in contradiction to the ideology, constitution and charter of *jahiliyyah*. The messengers neither gave such a response nor acted in such a manner as some ignorant people of our age say: merge into the *jahili* society, work from within, and spread your creed inside it.

The reality is that when the people of *da'wah* rise in a *jahili* society with a new Islamic ideology, then on the basis of that ideology their society, their leadership and their loyalties automatically separate. This is a natural matter; no one's intention plays a part in it. This natural and necessary process is inherent in the formation of any society. If, as a result of this process, a reaction arises within a *jahili* society because people are being gathered upon the worship, sovereignty, law, constitution and charter of One God alone, then this reaction too is natural. All the cogs of that *jahili* system then work again against Islam. If any Muslim becomes a cog in that *jahili* society, then in reality he will be a servant of that *jahili* society, not of Islam, just as some fools think: become a cog of *jahiliyyah* and serve Islam.

After this comes the reality that is destined for every *da'wah*, and for everyone who carries out the work of the Islamic *da'wah* in any time or place. It is this: Allah has promised His friends help, and He has surely said that My help will come and they will be given authority on earth. This promise will not take the form of reality until they are distinguished from a *jahili* society and separate from it, and until, on the basis of this *da'wah*, they separate from their people and form their own society and their own community. If they remain a part of a *jahili* society, moving about within it and being its cogs, then even though they hold the Islamic way of life as their belief and work for it, the fulfilment of Allah's help and promise will be delayed. This is the indispensable, great and fundamental condition, which those who carry out the work of Islamic *da'wah* must fully fulfil. They must understand this well.

Finally, there is another aspect worthy of reflection: how beautifully the Qur'an presents this caravan of the noble messengers. This caravan has been confronting *jahiliyyah* throughout human history with remarkable beauty and steadfastness. This portrayal is beautiful because the truth carried by the travellers of this caravan is extremely simple, natural and beautiful. These travellers are content, serious, and walking on their path with ....

﴿قَالَتْ لَهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ إِن نَّحْنُ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَمُنُّ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ﴾ ... ﴿فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ (14:11) "Their messengers said to them: 'Indeed, we are nothing but humans like you, but Allah bestows His favour upon whom He wills among His servants.' And it is not for us to bring you any authority, except by Allah's leave; and upon Allah let the believers rely."

This dazzling beauty arises because this is a single, unified caravan which, in every time and place, has confronted a unified *jahiliyyah*, in every age and in every nation.

Then this beauty appears to us from another angle as well: the deep connection between this *da'wah* and the truth carried by these noble messengers, and the truth hidden in this universe, because the messengers say:

﴿أَفِي اللَّهِ شَكٌّ فَاطِرِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ (14:10) "Is there doubt about Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth?" And in another verse:

﴿وَمَا لَنَا أَلَّا نَتَوَكَّلَ عَلَى اللَّهِ وَقَدْ هَدَانَا سُبُلَنَا﴾ (14:12) "And why should we not rely upon Allah, when He has guided us in our ways?" And elsewhere:

﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ ۚ إِن يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ وَيَأْتِ بِخَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ * وَمَا ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ بِعَزِيزٍ﴾ (14:19–20) "Do you not see that Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth? If He wills, He can remove you and bring a new creation. And that is not difficult for Allah."

Thus a deep connection is established between this cosmic truth and the truth of the Islamic *da'wah*, and from this it becomes clear that the Divine Being, who is the Truth, is the source of both these truths, and that these truths are deeply established, firm, and have roots reaching far into this universe.

﴿وَمَثَلُ كَلِمَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ كَشَجَرَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ ... مَا لَهَا مِن قَرَارٍ﴾ (14:26) "And the likeness of an evil word is that of an evil tree, uprooted from the earth's surface; it has no stability."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 14, verse 28–30:

Lesson No. 115: Explanation of the Verses 28 to 52

This is the second section of Surah Ibrahim. It takes up the same themes as the first section, is in harmony with it, and continues it. The subject of the first part was that Muhammad (ﷺ) has been sent as a Messenger so that he may bring people out of darkness into light. Moses (peace be upon him) was also sent for this same purpose: to bring his people out of darkness into light, and to admonish them that the punishment of Allah is very severe. Allah bestowed great favour upon the Children of Israel and declared that if they gave thanks, He would increase His blessings upon them, and if they were ungrateful, His punishment is severe. The circumstances of His Prophets and the end of the rebellious ones who denied them were presented. This narrative began, then went out of the context, and its various links kept appearing, along with various scenes, until the disbelievers reached the field of the Resurrection, where they heard the sermon of Satan, but this was after the time for it had passed. In the Hereafter, what sense is there in a sermon?

Having staged this long story of the Messengers, the discourse now comes to Muhammad (ﷺ) and his people: it is a great bounty of Allah that He has sent the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to bring people out of the darknesses into the light. This was a tremendous blessing from Allah, and the Messenger of Allah calls you so that Allah will forgive you. Yet your response is the same: you are ungrateful for this blessing, you reject this call, you adopt disbelief, and you prefer disbelief and ingratitude over the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his call.

After this, the blessings and favours of Allah upon all of humanity are enumerated. Examples are drawn from the open cosmic scenes, and as examples of gratitude for Allah's blessing, those who invited people to offer prayer while giving thanks to Allah are presented, and to do good to the servants of Allah, before the day comes in which there will be no material benefit, no buying and selling, and only friendship and intimacy will be of no use.

The question was: why does Allah not seize these disbelievers? Allah has neither left their matter aimless, nor is Allah heedless; rather, Allah is deferring their matter until the day of a punishment in which eyes will remain fixed in terror. As for the matter that the promise Allah made to His Messengers will certainly be fulfilled, even if the disbelievers devise their plots, and even if their plotting is so great that it could overturn even the great mountains. Thus this second section too becomes connected and continuous with the first.

Verses 28 to 30

What a strange situation: Allah has bestowed upon a people a great blessing in the form of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This Messenger carries a great call. It is a call to faith and righteous deeds. As a result, the whole people can attain success and forgiveness, and enter Paradise. Yet the people, instead of readily embracing this blessing, are adopting disbelief, and the leaders of that people, in whose hands is the reins of the ignorant masses, are steering the nation's leadership towards the pit of destruction rather than Paradise. The truth is that this is the condition of every nation: it is its leaders, who raise it up or cast it down. The leaders of the people of Muhammad (ﷺ) are also bringing people to the edge of the mouth of Hell and then arranging for them to fall into it and remain there, just as the ignorance-stricken leaders opposing earlier Prophets did the same to their nations. Just as those people brought ruin upon their nations, so too the people of Makkah are doing the same.

It is a strange act for the leaders of a nation, although they have read and seen the history of the peoples of earlier times. And if they had not seen and read it, then see how the Qur'an has staged this end in such an effective and dramatic manner. Its scenes have just passed before their eyes, and these scenes were so vivid that they seemed to be alive, and soon they will see them practically in the same way, because the texts of the Qur'an present scenes that are about to happen. It is only that the Qur'an presents them in such an impactful and captivating manner that it is as though they have already occurred. In short, the astonishing aspect of the conduct of these people is that in exchange for this blessing they are buying disbelief, and they are rejecting the call to Tawhid that is being given to them.

*"And they set up rivals to Allah, so that they might lead [people] astray from His way"* (14:30). That is, they make other beings equal to Allah, and they worship them in the same manner in which Allah is worshipped. They accept their sovereignty in the same way that Allah's sovereignty is accepted. They ascribe to these other beings attributes in the same way as the attributes of Allah, although Allah has no partner and no like. They have set up these partners for the purpose of leading people astray from Allah the One and from the Straight Path, because apart from the way of Allah, whatever paths they tread will be satanic paths.

This verse points to the fact that the great ones and leaders of the people deliberately led this nation astray from the way of Allah, and instead of declaring Allah the one true God, they handed the people over to other gods for leadership. Why? Because under the guise of these other gods, these people also display their leadership and dominance, whereas the doctrine of Tawhid is a threat to every rebellious dictator's leadership and to his interests. In every age and every society, this has been the attitude of the forces of tyranny. Just as this was the case in the ignorance of earlier times, so too in the ignorance of the modern age it is the same: people, in some form or another, abandon the doctrine of Tawhid and hand over their leadership to some tyrannical force. In the modern age, people hand over their freedom and liberty to such tyrannical gods. They follow their desires, take law and Shariah from them, and take laws and directives from these great ones instead of from the law of Allah. When the doctrine of Tawhid is extended to the meaning that the sovereign is Allah and the lawgiver is also Allah, then the leaders of the modern age, like the tyrannical forces of the first ignorance, come into the field against the Islamic movement. They consider the Islamic movement a threat to their own divinity, and they try in every way to protect themselves from it. The truth is that just as people today take law from other than Allah through parliament or ordinance, which contradicts the commands of Allah, and even make lawful what Allah has made unlawful and make unlawful what Allah has made lawful, so these people too are in fact committing shirk, and such leaders and lawmakers claim to be partners of Allah. And in this way people are led astray.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is told to say plainly to his people: enjoy yourselves, your days are few; when this respite ends, you and your such leadership will all be consigned to Hell.

*"O Messenger, leave them to their present state and now admonish My servants who have believed, who value Allah's blessing and do not deny it, who do not sell Allah's blessing in exchange for disbelief, so that they may give thanks to Me, worship Me, and obey Me."* Leaving these disbelievers aside, you should devote your full attention to the people of Islam.

Lesson No. 115: Explanation of the Verses 28 to 52

This is the second section of Surah Ibrahim. It takes up the same themes as the first section, is in harmony with it, and continues it. The subject of the first part was that Muhammad (ﷺ) has been sent as a Messenger so that he may bring people out of darkness into light. Moses (peace be upon him) was also sent for this same purpose: to bring his people out of darkness into light, and to admonish them that the punishment of Allah is very severe. Allah bestowed great favour upon the Children of Israel and declared that if they gave thanks, He would increase His blessings upon them, and if they were ungrateful, His punishment is severe. The circumstances of His Prophets and the end of the rebellious ones who denied them were presented. This narrative began, then went out of the context, and its various links kept appearing, along with various scenes, until the disbelievers reached the field of the Resurrection, where they heard the sermon of Satan, but this was after the time for it had passed. In the Hereafter, what sense is there in a sermon?

Having staged this long story of the Messengers, the discourse now comes to Muhammad (ﷺ) and his people: it is a great bounty of Allah that He has sent the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to bring people out of the darknesses into the light. This was a tremendous blessing from Allah, and the Messenger of Allah calls you so that Allah will forgive you. Yet your response is the same: you are ungrateful for this blessing, you reject this call, you adopt disbelief, and you prefer disbelief and ingratitude over the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his call.

After this, the blessings and favours of Allah upon all of humanity are enumerated. Examples are drawn from the open cosmic scenes, and as examples of gratitude for Allah's blessing, those who invited people to offer prayer while giving thanks to Allah are presented, and to do good to the servants of Allah, before the day comes in which there will be no material benefit, no buying and selling, and only friendship and intimacy will be of no use.

The question was: why does Allah not seize these disbelievers? Allah has neither left their matter aimless, nor is Allah heedless; rather, Allah is deferring their matter until the day of a punishment in which eyes will remain fixed in terror. As for the matter that the promise Allah made to His Messengers will certainly be fulfilled, even if the disbelievers devise their plots, and even if their plotting is so great that it could overturn even the great mountains. Thus this second section too becomes connected and continuous with the first.

Verse 31

Tell My servants to establish prayer (iqamat as-salah) as a way of expressing gratitude to Me. Prayer is the most specific way of giving thanks to God. Then, an important way of expressing My gratitude is spending in the way of Allah (infaq fi sabilillah) from what I have given them, both openly and secretly. Secretly is best when the aim is to protect the self-respect of those who receive, and also to preserve the dignity of those who give, because those who spend for show, for display, and for competition are not spending in the way of Allah. And spending openly is appropriate where the aim is to discharge obligatory charity (sadaqat wajibah), and where the aim is to make spending an exemplary model. The choice between these two methods is left to the conscience of the one who chooses.

And tell them as well that spending too has a time, a respite. When that respite ends, there will be no trade, wealth will not grow, friendships will not avail, and there will be nothing in hand for spending. There, only good deeds will be of use.

"Before there comes a Day in which there is no trading, nor any friendship" (14:31). Now Allah, opening the great book of this universe, enumerates His blessings. These are great and countless blessings. This book has large pages, and within them are blessings of every kind and hue, as far as the eye can see: the wide-spreading heavens, this earth, the sun and the moon, the alternation of night and day, the water that descends from the sky, the varieties of plants that grow from the earth, the seas, sea creatures and seafaring, the rivers, streams and waterways of the earth; in short, everything that man sees night and day. Yet people, because of their ignorance and jahiliyyah, do not read these pages, nor do they reflect upon them. Indeed, man is wrongdoing and ungrateful; he abandons the blessings of Allah for disbelief, and he associates partners with Allah, although Allah alone is the Creator and Provider, and it is He who has subjected this entire universe to man.

This is a passage from Sayyid Qutb's commentary, which I will translate in full below.

**Verses 32–34**

This is a powerful critical assault; whips are being lashed upon the human consciousness. The great celestial bodies and mountains of the heavens and earth, the sun and moon, the alternation of night and day, the rains and the fruits—all of these are performing the function of whips and stone-throwing. In them there is both a sharp sting for the consciousness of this wrongdoing human being, and also a loving and deeply moving voice.

The truth is that, for people of reflection, one of the miracles of this Book is that it joins the scenes of this universe and the perplexities of the human soul to the belief in Tawhid (the Oneness of God). This Book gives every scene and every radiance of this universe a suggestive hue. Likewise, it invites one to draw indications from every illumination among the thoughts and inspirations of the human soul. Thus this Book turns the whole universe into an exhibition hall of the signs and proofs of Allah, in which the wonders of the Divine Power are arranged everywhere. On every scene and every stall, the marvels of Divine Power are heaped up. In every thought, every color, and every shadow, nothing but Power is seen. The Qur'an does not begin the question of the existence of the Creator with a logical debate containing the theological and mundane discussions of ... Rather, it presents this matter in a highly effective, suggestive manner, and presents it in a most beautiful way and in a most logical order through the scenes of the universe, its wonders, and natural, engaging and self-evident things.

This is a grand and full scene, whose vistas move along the line in which the bounties and favours of Allah upon His servants are shown. These are wondrous examples of the craftsmanship of Divine Power. Along this line, first come the vast distances of the heavens and earth and their countless wonders. Then come the scenes of rains and their results, plants, fruits and produce, and all this comes into being through water upon the earth. Then along this path, before us appear the views of the seas in which ships and vessels sail, carrying the needs of people. Then before us appears a new view related to the sun, the moon and the earth, in which their movement and the resulting alternation of night and day are seen, and finally a collective glimpse of all these blessings, in which every need and desire of man and its fulfilment is displayed.

*And He gave you of all that you asked of Him* (14:34). Now the question is put: despite all these things, you still associate others with Allah. How cruel is your estimation and judgement, that you worship a lowly creature of the heavens and earth among the creatures of Allah.

*And sent down water from the sky, and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you* (14:32). Agriculture is the greatest and first source of human sustenance, and all outward blessings are connected with agriculture. Rain and the resulting growth of vegetation are subject to the law of nature which Allah has established on this earth. This law of nature sends rains, grows vegetation, and from it various kinds of fruits are produced, and all these conveniences and facilities are for man. In the formation and provision of a single grain of sustenance, a number of factors operate, such as earth, water, the rays of the sun and air. People, on hearing the word *rizq* (provision), think only of the final form of wealth and property, whereas many things fall within the scope of human sustenance, and the whole system of sustenance is very profound. For the establishment of human life on this earth, the universe moves great celestial bodies in order to supply at least what is needed. Within this a very profound law of nature operates, and thousands of facilities and conveniences are provided which work together in harmony. Only then is the minimum standard for sustaining human life fulfilled. If even one of these conveniences were absent, the very survival of this human being would become impossible and his existence would not be. The bodies mentioned in this verse, whose movement and service are said to supply the means of man's sustenance, are sufficient and complete, and all of them belong to the Divine Power.

*And subjected to you the ships to sail through the sea by His command* (14:32). For it is Allah who placed in the elements those properties by which the ship moves upon the waters, and gave man such rational faculties that he learned these matters. All these works man can do by the command of Allah.

*And subjected to you the rivers* (14:32). By causing these rivers to flow, streams of life began to flow and springs of goodness burst forth for mankind. Then in these rivers are fish and other good things; all these things Allah created for man. Whether birds or beasts, man benefits from them.

*And subjected to you the sun and the moon, both constant in their courses* (14:33). Man cannot benefit directly from the sun and moon in the way he benefits directly from water, crops and fruits, from seas, ships, canals and rivers; but the effects of the sun and moon are beneficial for man. From them man draws the material of life and gains strength, because Allah has bound them to a law of nature such that they continually supply man's needs. The needs of human life and the cells of the human body are composed, renewed and transformed by these rays of the sun.

*And subjected to you the night and the day* (14:33). Allah made these in accordance with human need. The present system of the alternation of night and day is absolutely necessary for human life on this earth and for its activities. If there were always day, or always night, man could not survive at all. The environment of the earth would become unfavourable to him, and this life, these developments and this produce would become difficult.

These are only the outlines of Allah's countless blessings. If each point within these outlines were to be discussed one by one, it would become a separate book. For this reason Allah here gathers them up in summary.

A principle matter: *And gave you of all that you asked of Him* — wealth, children, health, equipment and so on.

*And if you should count the favour of Allah, you could not enumerate them* (14:34). They are so numerous that even a great multitude of people could not count them; indeed, even if all of mankind were to labour at it, they could not count them. This is because man is limited within time and space, his knowledge is limited, it has a beginning and an end, and it is confined between time and space, whereas Allah's blessings are so vast that they lie beyond the sphere of human knowledge and perception. Despite all these truths, O people, you still set up partners with Allah, and knowing all this, you do not give thanks for Allah's blessings, but instead of gratitude you commit disbelief. The truth is:

*Indeed, mankind is {\it extremely} unjust and ungrateful* (14:34). When the human conscience awakens and begins to see the universe around it with a seeing eye, it sees that this whole universe has been subjected to it: either directly under its control, or in such a way that, by the law of nature established by Allah, it works for man and supplies man's needs. When man reflects upon his environment in this way, he comes to realize that by the mercy and compassion of Allah this whole environment is man's friend and helper, and Allah has made it very gentle and obedient to man. Then man's conscience awakens. When he raises his head and looks at his environment with a reflective gaze, he begins to tremble; he fears Allah, falls in prostration, and gives thanks to Allah. Then, in humility and submission, he looks toward his Lord, the Bestower. If he is in some difficulty, he prays for ease; and if he is immersed in Allah's blessings, he prays that Allah keep these blessings safe and continuing.

And the supreme example of one who remembers, gives thanks and reflects is Abu al-Anbiya, Hadrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him), after whom this surah is named. This is the reason why the themes and atmosphere of this surah also revolve around the axis of gratitude, ingratitude and denial of blessings. Thus Hadrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him) is presented in his noble character in which he is the embodiment of gratitude. He is in a state of deep humility and submission, and with a very soft and gentle murmur he raises his hands in supplication. The murmur of his prayers and gratitude rises toward the sky in the form of very gentle and respectful waves, and its echo reaches far, disappearing into the heavens.
