The bodies mentioned in this verse, whose movement and service are said to supply the means of man's sustenance, are sufficient and complete, and all of them belong to the Divine Power.

*And subjected to you the ships to sail through the sea by His command* (14:32). For it is Allah who placed in the elements those properties by which the ship moves upon the waters, and gave man such rational faculties that he learned these matters. All these works man can do by the command of Allah.

*And subjected to you the rivers* (14:32). By causing these rivers to flow, streams of life began to flow and springs of goodness burst forth for mankind. Then in these rivers are fish and other good things; all these things Allah created for man. Whether birds or beasts, man benefits from them.

*And subjected to you the sun and the moon, both constant in their courses* (14:33). Man cannot benefit directly from the sun and moon in the way he benefits directly from water, crops and fruits, from seas, ships, canals and rivers; but the effects of the sun and moon are beneficial for man. From them man draws the material of life and gains strength, because Allah has bound them to a law of nature such that they continually supply man's needs. The needs of human life and the cells of the human body are composed, renewed and transformed by these rays of the sun.

*And subjected to you the night and the day* (14:33). Allah made these in accordance with human need. The present system of the alternation of night and day is absolutely necessary for human life on this earth and for its activities. If there were always day, or always night, man could not survive at all. The environment of the earth would become unfavourable to him, and this life, these developments and this produce would become difficult.

These are only the outlines of Allah's countless blessings. If each point within these outlines were to be discussed one by one, it would become a separate book. For this reason Allah here gathers them up in summary.

A principle matter: *And gave you of all that you asked of Him* — wealth, children, health, equipment and so on.

*And if you should count the favour of Allah, you could not enumerate them* (14:34). They are so numerous that even a great multitude of people could not count them; indeed, even if all of mankind were to labour at it, they could not count them. This is because man is limited within time and space, his knowledge is limited, it has a beginning and an end, and it is confined between time and space, whereas Allah's blessings are so vast that they lie beyond the sphere of human knowledge and perception. Despite all these truths, O people, you still set up partners with Allah, and knowing all this, you do not give thanks for Allah's blessings, but instead of gratitude you commit disbelief. The truth is:

*Indeed, mankind is {\it extremely} unjust and ungrateful* (14:34). When the human conscience awakens and begins to see the universe around it with a seeing eye, it sees that this whole universe has been subjected to it: either directly under its control, or in such a way that, by the law of nature established by Allah, it works for man and supplies man's needs. When man reflects upon his environment in this way, he comes to realize that by the mercy and compassion of Allah this whole environment is man's friend and helper, and Allah has made it very gentle and obedient to man. Then man's conscience awakens. When he raises his head and looks at his environment with a reflective gaze, he begins to tremble; he fears Allah, falls in prostration, and gives thanks to Allah. Then, in humility and submission, he looks toward his Lord, the Bestower. If he is in some difficulty, he prays for ease; and if he is immersed in Allah's blessings, he prays that Allah keep these blessings safe and continuing.

And the supreme example of one who remembers, gives thanks and reflects is Abu al-Anbiya, Hadrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him), after whom this surah is named. This is the reason why the themes and atmosphere of this surah also revolve around the axis of gratitude, ingratitude and denial of blessings. Thus Hadrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him) is presented in his noble character in which he is the embodiment of gratitude. He is in a state of deep humility and submission, and with a very soft and gentle murmur he raises his hands in supplication. The murmur of his prayers and gratitude rises toward the sky in the form of very gentle and respectful waves, and its echo reaches far, disappearing into the heavens.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 14, verses 35–41 (part 1 of 2):

Verses 35 to 41

In this scene, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) is seen standing beside the House of Allah. He has built the Ka'bah, and this is the same House whose custodianship has now come down to the Quraysh. Just look at them: they commit disbelief (kufr) in Allah within the House of Allah. And they commit this disbelief in the very house whose builder had constructed it solely for the worship of Allah. In this scene the Qur'an presents Ibrahim (peace be upon him) as a humble man, one who fears Allah greatly, and one who remembers and gives thanks. This is so that the Quraysh may reflect, abandon their denial and obstinacy, acknowledge the call of Islam, be thankful instead of disbelieving, take admonition instead of being heedless, and, along with their claim to be the progeny of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), return to the true path from which they have strayed, and follow the way of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) to attain the path of guidance.

﴿Our Lord, make this city (i.e., Makkah) a city of security﴾ (14:35). Security is a blessing that every human being needs. Security has a profound effect on human feelings, for human life can only continue in peace. Here the prayer of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) for security is brought forward so that the people of Makkah may be told: use your intellect, and do not destroy the security of this city. It was obtained after great supplications. For a long time you have benefited from it, yet you destroy it with your own hands and do not give thanks. This security has been granted to this city through the prayers of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Alas, a thousand alases, that you have abandoned the way and religion of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and thus you are ungrateful. And, in addition to this, you have placed idols of Allah's partners in this House of Monotheism; you bar people in this city from the religion of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and from the path of Allah. Reflect upon this part of the prayer of Ibrahim (peace be upon him).

﴿And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols﴾ (14:35). From this prayer of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) it becomes clear that he is a embodiment of submission and contentment before his Lord, and he is pleading from the depths of his heart. The prayer is: O Allah, keep me and my offspring away from idol worship. He seeks both help in his prayer and guidance. From this prayer it becomes clear that he regards this guidance as one of the blessings of Allah, through which the heart emerges from the darkness of polytheism and idol worship, and in place of ignorance it gains knowledge, and in place of darkness it gains light. That is, the guidance and light of faith in Allah and monotheism. Ultimately, through monotheism, a person emerges from the layers of bewilderment and anxiety and escapes from misguidance and wickedness. He becomes enlightened, tranquil and steadfast, and, leaving the servitude of many gods and lords, and leaving humiliation and slavery, he enters the most honourable servitude of one God and attains a free life. These are the blessings that the Lord had bestowed upon Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Now he prays that these blessings may remain: that he and his descendants may remain far from the curse of idol worship.

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) makes this prayer because he sees that in his environment, among the majority of his contemporary generations, idol worship has misguided them, and that earlier peoples too were afflicted by it, and that the idols have misled a great multitude.

﴿My Lord, they have indeed led many of the people astray﴾ (14:36). Now this prayer takes on the tone of a declaration. He says: whoever follows my way will be mine, will be able to be attributed to me, and on the Day of Resurrection will be among my companions, a companion in faith and conviction.

﴿So whoever follows me is of me﴾ (14:36). And whoever abandons my way, his outcome I entrust to You.

﴿And whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (14:36). From this it becomes clear how merciful, compassionate, forbearing and patient Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was. Therefore he does not demand the destruction of those people who do not adopt the ways of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and who turn aside. He does not hasten punishment for them; rather he does not even mention punishment. He entrusts those who turn away from his ways to the mercy and kindness of Allah, to pardon and forgiveness. Thus the atmosphere is spread with shadows of mercy and forgiveness, and as a result of these shadows of compassion, kindness and recognition, the atmosphere of disobedience is suppressed. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) does not open up the atmosphere of disobedience; he sends it into the background.

Now, after this, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) presents before Allah the request that, O Allah, You see that I have settled some of my offspring permanently in this barren valley, which is barren and destitute except for its nearness to the Sacred House, and he also makes clear the purpose of settling these people here.

﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in an uncultivated valley near Your Sacred House﴾ (14:37). Why? 

﴿Our Lord, that they may establish prayer﴾ (14:37). Our Lord, I have done this so that these people establish prayer here. The establishment of prayer alone is the purpose, and solely for this purpose they have been settled in this barren and dry valley.

﴿So make hearts among the people incline toward them﴾ (14:37). There is such tenderness in this prayer and such delight in the atmosphere. Tenderness arises in the heart, and eager beholders are seen swooping like moths upon this city. Caravans of lovers are moving toward this uncultivated, dry and barren valley. In short, there is such freshness within this prayer and such tenderness in it that it is almost as if the tears of the entire universe would drench this valley.

﴿And provide for them from the fruits﴾ (14:37). And these fruits should reach them through those who fall upon this House and upon these people from every direction like moths. Why? So that they may eat, drink and enjoy, and after that, as the desire of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) for them to be grateful is evident, this is it.

﴿That they may be grateful﴾ (14:37). Thus Ibrahim (peace be upon him) settles his offspring in the vicinity of the Sacred House, and the context of the speech shows that its purpose is precisely that they should establish prayers there, in the manner in which prayer is to be established. Moreover, the purpose of this prayer of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) appears to be that the desire behind it is solely the impulse that people should be grateful to Allah. The hearts of people should be drawn toward the House of Allah and its people, and then from this gathering of people, provision in the form of fruits and grains should be supplied to them, and in return these people should give thanks to Allah.

In the light of this prayer, the Qur'an makes clear the truth that the Quraysh, for which purpose they were settled near the House of Allah, have abandoned that purpose. They neither establish prayer for Allah nor give thanks to Allah for these blessings, although the prayer of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) has been accepted. The gathering of people at the House of Allah continues, and fruits and produce are arriving in abundance from every direction.

Ibrahim (peace be upon him), upon this prayer that He has settled his offspring here and that provision and other necessities be supplied to them, so that they may establish prayer and give thanks to Allah, now himself comments: Allah knows the desires of all people, whether apparent or hidden. If someone prays out of fear of God and gives thanks, Allah knows it. In attention to Allah, outward displays have no importance, just as these people clap and whistle in the House of Allah. Worship and prayer are truly that in which the heart and conscience of a person turn toward Allah, for nothing of anyone is hidden from Allah. He knows whatever is manifest and hidden in the heavens and the earth.

﴿Our Lord, indeed You know what we conceal and what we reveal﴾ (14:38). And indeed, nothing is hidden from Allah, neither in the earth nor in the heavens.

After this, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) recalls the earlier favours of Allah and gives thanks and praise.

﴿All praise is due to Allah, who has granted me, in old age, Isma'il and Ishaq. Indeed my Lord is the Hearer of supplication﴾ (14:39). If someone is granted children in old age when previously he had none, it has a great effect upon him, for children are in fact the continuity of human life. If a person's life is nearing its end and he unexpectedly receives children, this is an extremely reassuring matter, because the human self always feels the need to have offspring. This is why Ibrahim praises the Lord and hopes for further mercy from Allah.

Now, after this thanks and praise, he prays that O Allah, grant me constancy in giving thanks and in praising the Lord, so that I may continue to worship You and obey You. Thus Ibrahim (peace be upon him) expresses his resolve that he will continue to give thanks and continue to worship Allah, and he makes this prayer out of fear that some obstacle may arise, that some matter may turn him away from it. Therefore he now also prays that Allah, by His help, keep this resolve going.

﴿My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [among] my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication﴾ (14:40). Once again we see a complete contrast between Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and his descendants, the Quraysh. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) seeks help from Allah so that He makes him an establisher of prayer and grants both him and his offspring the ability to do this, yet his descendants turn away from prayer. And the messenger who came to them from among the descendants of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who admonishes them and reminds them of the teachings of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), these people are determined to deny him, although he is one of them.

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) concludes this prayer, full of humility, submission and lowliness, by seeking forgiveness for himself, for his parents and for all believers: O Allah, forgive us on the Day of Reckoning, for on the Day of Reckoning a person will benefit only from his deeds, or else forgiveness from Allah alone will do his work.

﴿Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the day the account is established﴾ (14:41). Here the scene of this prayer, full of submission and humility, comes to an end, in which the unbounded blessings of Allah and the scenes of gratitude for them were shown. The tone of the discourse was that of a very gentle music, like the faint ripples that rise on the surface of water in a light breeze. This scene casts over the whole atmosphere a tender and farewell-like emotional mood. Human hearts come under the shelter of Allah, recall His blessings, and this scene portrays Ibrahim (peace be upon him) as a servant who remembers and gives thanks, just as before this prayer the Qur'an had called all the servants of Allah to become servants who remember and give thanks.

Let the readers not forget to note here that in this heartrending prayer of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), the words "Rabbana", "Rabb" and "Rabbi" are used. He has deliberately employed the attribute of lordship (rububiyyah) for himself and, after him, for his offspring, and there is deep wisdom hidden in this. He does not bring here the attribute of divinity (uluhiyyah) but the attribute of lordship, because in all the jahiliyyahs, especially the Arab jahiliyyah, the divinity of Allah has not been disputed. What has always been in dispute is the lordship of Allah. That is, the Lord is the one whose prescribed system, religion and law operate on this earth, and this is the real practical issue which affects people's lives. It is on account of this that Islam and jahiliyyah are distinguished, and monotheism is separated from polytheism, because people will either be within the religion of Allah, in which case Allah is their Lord, or they will be within the system of other than Allah, in which case that other than Allah becomes their lord. This is the difference between Islam and jahiliyyah, and between monotheism and polytheism, which in practical life separates Islam from jahiliyyah and monotheism from polytheism. The Qur'an presents here, in the prayer of their forefather Ibrahim (peace be upon him), the issue of lordship to the Quraysh, and it emphasises lordship precisely because it wishes to make clear to the Arabs and the Quraysh that you are going against the testament and prayers of your revered ancestor.

At the beginning of this section in the context of the discourse, the following verses were presented:

﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for ingratitude and made their people settle in the abode of destruction?﴾ (14:28). These people remained steadfast in their own unjust scheme, yet the punishment of Allah did not descend upon them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was commanded to say to them:

"Say: Enjoy yourselves, for your final destination is the Fire" (14:30). And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was further commanded to turn the direction of his call toward the believers, to urge them to prayer and to spending (infaq) in charity, both openly and secretly.

"Before there comes a Day in which there will be no trading, nor any friendship" (14:31). Now the discussion of this section is completed with regard to those who are ungrateful for the blessings of Allah: what Allah has prepared for them, when they will reach this end, and this matter is described in the form of scenes of the Day of Resurrection, which come one after another, in which human feet slip out of fear and hearts tremble violently.

This is so that the Quraysh may reflect, abandon their denial and obstinacy, acknowledge the call of Islam, be thankful instead of disbelieving, take admonition instead of being heedless, and, along with their claim to be the progeny of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), return to the true path from which they have strayed, and follow the way of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) to attain the path of guidance.

﴿Our Lord, make this city (i.e., Makkah) a city of security﴾ (14:35). Security is a blessing that every human being needs. This security has been granted to this city through the prayers of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Reflect upon this part of the prayer of Ibrahim (peace be upon him).

From this prayer of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) it becomes clear that he is a embodiment of submission and contentment before his Lord, and he is pleading from the depths of his heart. From this prayer it becomes clear that he regards this guidance as one of the blessings of Allah, through which the heart emerges from the darkness of polytheism and idol worship, and in place of ignorance it gains knowledge, and in place of darkness it gains light. He becomes enlightened, tranquil and steadfast, and, leaving the servitude of many gods and lords, and leaving humiliation and slavery, he enters the most honourable servitude of one God and attains a free life. These are the blessings that the Lord had bestowed upon Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Now he prays that these blessings may remain: that he and his descendants may remain far from the curse of idol worship.

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) makes this prayer because he sees that in his environment, among the majority of his contemporary generations, idol worship has misguided them, and that earlier peoples too were afflicted by it, and that the idols have misled a great multitude.

﴿My Lord, they have indeed led many of the people astray﴾ (14:36). Now this prayer takes on the tone of a declaration. He says: whoever follows my way will be mine, will be able to be attributed to me, and on the Day of Resurrection will be among my companions, a companion in faith and conviction.

﴿And whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (14:36). From this it becomes clear how merciful, compassionate, forbearing and patient Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was. Therefore he does not demand the destruction of those people who do not adopt the ways of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and who turn aside. He does not hasten punishment for them; rather he does not even mention punishment. He entrusts those who turn away from his ways to the mercy and kindness of Allah, to pardon and forgiveness. Thus the atmosphere is spread with shadows of mercy and forgiveness, and as a result of these shadows of compassion, kindness and recognition, the atmosphere of disobedience is suppressed. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) does not open up the atmosphere of disobedience; he sends it into the background.

Now, after this, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) presents before Allah the request that, O Allah, You see that I have settled some of my offspring permanently in this barren valley, which is barren and destitute except for its nearness to the Sacred House, and he also makes clear the purpose of settling these people here.

﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in an uncultivated valley near Your Sacred House﴾ (14:37). Why? 

﴿Our Lord, that they may establish prayer﴾ (14:37). Our Lord, I have done this so that these people establish prayer here. The establishment of prayer alone is the purpose, and solely for this purpose they have been settled in this barren and dry valley.

﴿So make hearts among the people incline toward them﴾ (14:37). There is such tenderness in this prayer and such delight in the atmosphere. Tenderness arises in the heart, and eager beholders are seen swooping like moths upon this city. Caravans of lovers are moving toward this uncultivated, dry and barren valley. In short, there is such freshness within this prayer and such tenderness in it that it is almost as if the tears of the entire universe would drench this valley.

﴿And provide for them from the fruits﴾ (14:37). And these fruits should reach them through those who fall upon this House and upon these people from every direction like moths. Why? Moreover, the purpose of this prayer of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) appears to be that the desire behind it is solely the impulse that people should be grateful to Allah. The hearts of people should be drawn toward the House of Allah and its people, and then from this gathering of people, provision in the form of fruits and grains should be supplied to them, and in return these people should give thanks to Allah.

In the light of this prayer, the Qur'an makes clear the truth that the Quraysh, for which purpose they were settled near the House of Allah, have abandoned that purpose. They neither establish prayer for Allah nor give thanks to Allah for these blessings, although the prayer of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) has been accepted. The gathering of people at the House of Allah continues, and fruits and produce are arriving in abundance from every direction.

Ibrahim (peace be upon him), upon this prayer that He has settled his offspring here and that provision and other necessities be supplied to them, so that they may establish prayer and give thanks to Allah, now himself comments: Allah knows the desires of all people, whether apparent or hidden. If someone prays out of fear of God and gives thanks, Allah knows it. In attention to Allah, outward displays have no importance, just as these people clap and whistle in the House of Allah. Worship and prayer are truly that in which the heart and conscience of a person turn toward Allah, for nothing of anyone is hidden from Allah. He knows whatever is manifest and hidden in the heavens and the earth.

﴿Our Lord, indeed You know what we conceal and what we reveal﴾ (14:38). And indeed, nothing is hidden from Allah, neither in the earth nor in the heavens.

After this, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) recalls the earlier favours of Allah and gives thanks and praise.

﴿All praise is due to Allah, who has granted me, in old age, Isma'il and Ishaq. Indeed my Lord is the Hearer of supplication﴾ (14:39). If someone is granted children in old age when previously he had none, it has a great effect upon him, for children are in fact the continuity of human life. If a person's life is nearing its end and he unexpectedly receives children, this is an extremely reassuring matter, because the human self always feels the need to have offspring. This is why Ibrahim praises the Lord and hopes for further mercy from Allah.

Now, after this thanks and praise, he prays that O Allah, grant me constancy in giving thanks and in praising the Lord, so that I may continue to worship You and obey You. Thus Ibrahim (peace be upon him) expresses his resolve that he will continue to give thanks and continue to worship Allah, and he makes this prayer out of fear that some obstacle may arise, that some matter may turn him away from it. Therefore he now also prays that Allah, by His help, keep this resolve going.

Once again we see a complete contrast between Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and his descendants, the Quraysh. ﴿Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the day the account is established﴾ (14:41). Here the scene of this prayer, full of submission and humility, comes to an end, in which the unbounded blessings of Allah and the scenes of gratitude for them were shown. The tone of the discourse was that of a very gentle music, like the faint ripples that rise on the surface of water in a light breeze. This scene casts over the whole atmosphere a tender and farewell-like emotional mood. Human hearts come under the shelter of Allah, recall His blessings, and this scene portrays Ibrahim (peace be upon him) as a servant who remembers and gives thanks, just as before this prayer the Qur'an had called all the servants of Allah to become servants who remember and give thanks.

This scene casts over the whole atmosphere a tender and farewell-like emotional mood. Human hearts come under the shelter of Allah, recall His blessings, and this scene portrays Ibrahim (peace be upon him) as a servant who remembers and gives thanks, just as before this prayer the Qur'an had called all the servants of Allah to become servants who remember and give thanks.

Let the readers not forget to note here that in this heartrending prayer of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), the words "Rabbana", "Rabb" and "Rabbi" are used. He has deliberately employed the attribute of lordship (rububiyyah) for himself and, after him, for his offspring, and there is deep wisdom hidden in this. He does not bring here the attribute of divinity (uluhiyyah) but the attribute of lordship, because in all the jahiliyyahs, especially the Arab jahiliyyah, the divinity of Allah has not been disputed. What has always been in dispute is the lordship of Allah. That is, the Lord is the one whose prescribed system, religion and law operate on this earth, and this is the real practical issue which affects people's lives. It is on account of this that Islam and jahiliyyah are distinguished, and monotheism is separated from polytheism, because people will either be within the religion of Allah, in which case Allah is their Lord, or they will be within the system of other than Allah, in which case that other than Allah becomes their lord. This is the difference between Islam and jahiliyyah, and between monotheism and polytheism, which in practical life separates Islam from jahiliyyah and monotheism from polytheism. The Qur'an presents here, in the prayer of their forefather Ibrahim (peace be upon him), the issue of lordship to the Quraysh, and it emphasises lordship precisely because it wishes to make clear to the Arabs and the Quraysh that you are going against the testament and prayers of your revered ancestor.

At the beginning of this section in the context of the discourse, the following verses were presented:

﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for ingratitude and made their people settle in the abode of destruction?﴾ (14:28). These people remained steadfast in their own unjust scheme, yet the punishment of Allah did not descend upon them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was commanded to say to them:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 14, verses 35–41 (part 2 of 2):

"Say: Enjoy yourselves, for your final destination is the Fire" (14:30). And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was further commanded to turn the direction of his call toward the believers, to urge them to prayer and to spending (infaq) in charity, both openly and secretly.

"Before there comes a Day in which there will be no trading, nor any friendship" (14:31). Now the discussion of this section is completed with regard to those who are ungrateful for the blessings of Allah: what Allah has prepared for them, when they will reach this end, and this matter is described in the form of scenes of the Day of Resurrection, which come one after another, in which human feet slip out of fear and hearts tremble violently.

The Prophet ﷺ did not consider Allah to be unaware of the deeds of the wrongdoers. But apparently people would see that the wrongdoers were living in luxury, hearing Allah's threats, while the life of this world was passing, and no punishment of Allah was seizing those wrongdoers. Therefore Allah adopts this style of address so that it may be established with certainty that these people are advancing very swiftly towards the respite appointed for them. In the end, Allah seizes such people at the appointed time, and His seizure is such that no one can escape from it. It will be a severe day on which their gazes will remain fixed and wide open, and they will be in a state of extreme anguish and distress. Their eyes will be open, but their faculties will be stunned, and they will see nothing. There will be such terror that wherever their gaze settles, it will remain fixed there. And on that terrible day the condition of the whole nation will be such that they will run about in panic. Their attention will be on nothing. Their regard will be for nothing. They will have their heads raised, not out of joy but out of compulsion, their heads will be lifted upward. Whenever their gaze rises and fixes on any scene, they will be unable to turn it away, and their gaze will remain stuck there. Their hearts will be hollow, as if they are flying about. They will have no recollection, no argument or proof, and no plan.

This is the day to which Allah is postponing them. Thus they will stand in that field, utterly terrified. In these four parts of the verse, their condition appears just as a very small bird is caught in the talons of a powerful falcon (baz) and it seizes it. Please read again:

Innama yu'akhkhiruhum ... al-absar (42), Muhti'in ... wa af'idatuhum hawa' (43) (14:42–43). Allah is only deferring them to a day when their condition will be that their eyes are wide open and fixed, they are running with heads raised, their gazes are fixed upward, and their hearts are flying away.

Running swiftly with heads raised, with gazes fixed on the heavens in a fixed stare, and with the heart in a state where it flies like the wind and nothing is understood, this is a state in which extreme terror is displayed, in which a person's gaze becomes fixed on one spot.

This is the day to which Allah is taking them, and at which they are awaited at the end of their respite. So, O Prophet, warn these people of the day on which no excuse will be accepted and no way of escape will exist. Then another scene of that terrifying day is brought forward.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 14, verses 44–45:

Verses 44 to 45

O Messenger, warn these people of the punishment whose picture has just been drawn. On that day these wrongdoers will ask, full of hope and with an air of entitlement: "Rabbana" (O our Lord). Today they address Him with great deference as "Rabbana," whereas in the world they used to associate partners with Allah.

﴿Grant us respite for a little while; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers﴾ (14:44).

Here the narrative style takes the form of direct address. It is as though they are standing before us, looking on, making demands and offering supplications, while we are now in the place of Gathering (al-Mahshar). The record of worldly life has been rolled up, and look, from the higher realm they are being addressed directly, severely rebuked and deeply shamed, and reminded to look back at what they used to do.

﴿Did you not swear before, saying that there would be no decline for you?﴾ (14:44). Now, what is your opinion? Have you declined or not? You used to say such things while the traces and history of earlier nations lay before you. The end of the wrongdoers and rebels was clearly in front of you.

﴿And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it had become clear to you how We dealt with them, and We set forth examples for you﴾ (14:45). Yet your attitude was also strange: you saw the ruins of those wrongdoers and their circumstances, saw that their cities lay empty and that you were now living in their towns, and still you kept swearing, "There will be no decline for you." Here the scene ends, and we learn what became of them after their supplication was rejected.

The truth is that such situations occur day and night in our own lives. Many tyrants and dictators sit upon the thrones of those who came before them, and sometimes they are the very ones who were defeated and expelled at the hands of earlier tyrants in power. Yet despite this, these successors begin again with rebellion, oppression and domination, and walk exactly in the footsteps of their predecessors, taking the path of destruction. The cautionary histories of people who passed before them do not stir their consciousness or conscience, although their history is crying out. This is your history too. Then, when the punishment of Allah arrives, they are seized just like their predecessors, and they join them, meeting the same end, and Allah's earth is emptied of these impure people.

Now the curtain falls. The scene of the Resurrection is folded up, and the discussion turns to the present circumstances of those who lived in this world. These people were plotting against the Messenger ﷺ and the believers night and day, and in every field of life they were creating mischief against Islam. It is told that your deception, your scheming and your propaganda, however great they may be, Allah will seize you just as He seized the nations before you.

Verse 46

Allah encompasses them, and their plotting is within the sphere of Allah's power, even though their schemes may be so harsh and severe that by them mountains could be moved from their places. It is evident that to move a mountain from its place requires a very great force, which a human being cannot even imagine. Although they devise very great deceptions and cunning, none of their deceit lies outside the sphere of Allah's power; rather, Allah can nullify their machinations in whatever manner He wills.

This people's schemes are not effective against Allah, and when Allah wills to help His messengers and His movements, no one can stop Him. "Indeed, He is the Mighty, the Possessor of retribution."

No wrongdoer can escape from Him, and no schemer can be saved from His punishment. Here, the word "retribution" (intiqam) is brought in contrast with oppression, rebellion and great cunning, and it is most fitting, because it is appropriate to take retribution against the oppressor and the schemer. When retribution is attributed to Allah, it means the fitting reward and punishment for oppression and rebellion, and this too through a just method of action. And this just reward and punishment will indeed take place when...

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 14, verse 48:

How this will happen, we do not have the details of, nor do we know what the physics of that other earth will be like or where it will be. However, these verses of the Quran impress upon our consciousness the impression of what these people are and what their intrigues are. The power of Allah is such that He will change the earth and the heavens. Their achievements are petty and insignificant in comparison with Allah. Look, in the other scene, the earth and the heavens have been changed by the power of Allah!!

Verse 48

Translation: They will realize that they are standing before Allah bare and exposed. No one will save them. They are not in their homes! They are not even in their graves! They are standing in an open plain before Allah, the One, the Subduer. Here the word "Qahhar" (the Subduer) has been used deliberately, so that tyrants and dictators are warned that their tyranny counts for nothing before Allah, even if this tyranny and intrigue are so severe that mountains could be built from them.

Now before us is presented one of the intense and harsh scenes of the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, which is extremely humiliating and suitable for tyrants and oppressive schemers.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 14, verses 49–50:

Verses 49–50

The scene of these criminals is such that they will be bound together in pairs in chains. They will be marching in rows. This will be their humiliation from the side of Allah, the Subduer (Qahhar). Moreover, their garments will be made of a material that is highly flammable, and along with this it will be of black tar. This will be a further humiliation for them. The purpose is that as soon as they come near the fire, these people will become prey to the flames.

﴿وَتَغْشَىٰ وُجُوهَهُمُ ٱلنَّارُ﴾ (14:50) "And the Fire will cover their faces." This will be a humiliating punishment, and a fitting remedy for their deceit, their rebelliousness and their arrogance.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 14, verse 51:

Verse 51

They had made oppression and deceit their way of life, so a wrath from Allah will descend upon them and they will be humiliated. Allah is swift in reckoning. Given their deceit and their deep schemes, it is fitting that their reckoning be hastened, because they thought that Allah would not expose their deceit and that no power would be able to overcome them. So Allah will now swiftly take their account from them and punish them with utmost humiliation.

The surah concludes on the same theme with which it began, but this conclusion takes the form of a public proclamation, made openly so that this general announcement reaches all people everywhere.

This public proclamation has a basic purpose: that people should know that Allah is the one God and the sole Sovereign. This is the fundamental principle on which the Islamic system stands.

But the real aim of this proclamation is not merely abstract. The real objective is that people should establish their whole system of life on this principle and adopt obedience to Allah in their entire lives. If they consider Allah to be the one God and Sovereign, then, because whoever is regarded as God, Creator and Owner is also the Sovereign and Lord, He will also be the Head, the Disposer of affairs, the Director and the Lawgiver. If human life is practically established on this faith and proclamation, that practical system will be the complete opposite of a system established on the principle that some people shall be slaves to other similar people, and that among humans some shall be rulers, lawgivers and oppressors. This is a fundamental difference, because of which beliefs and concepts diverge, rites and forms of worship diverge, morals and conduct diverge, the standards of good and evil change, and political and economic systems change. In short, if a society is organised on any of these bases, its individual and collective features will themselves change.

The doctrine that Allah is one and is the Sovereign builds, on its foundation, a complete system of life. This doctrine is not one that remains only in minds. The Islamic outlook on life is not limited to beliefs; its boundaries extend far beyond them. This doctrine embraces the whole practical life of a human being. The doctrine of Allah's sovereignty is part of Islamic belief. The establishment of Islamic morality is also part of our beliefs. And this is a creed and outlook on life from which a complete system springs forth. New values come into existence, and it presents to the world new conditions and a new constitutional and legal system.

We cannot grasp the objectives and aims of the Qur'an until we understand well the Qur'anic beliefs and doctrines, and until we understand well the meaning of the testimony of faith (kalimah shahadah), what the true meaning of La ilaha illa Allah Muhammad Rasul Allah is, and until we understand its meaning with all its breadth. Until we understand what "worship" ('ibadah) means in Islam, and until we include in the definition of worship that it means obedience and servitude to Allah throughout life, not only at the times of prayer but in all affairs of life.

The idolatry of the Arabs, for which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) prayed for himself and his descendants, that Allah keep them away from it, was not as simple as the Arabs practised it in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), or as it was practised in various forms in other periods of ignorance, where trees and stones were worshipped, animals and birds were worshipped, stars and planets were worshipped, spirits and illusions were worshipped. These simple forms were not the whole of shirk, nor were these simple forms the whole of idol-worship, nor was shirk confined to these simple forms. Nor was this idolatry limited to this meaning, and beyond this we cannot discover other forms of shirk, or they simply do not exist. Rather, the reality is that the forms of shirk are countless, and we cannot confine our thinking to those forms, rather in the modern jahiliyyah countless new forms of shirk have also come into being.

Therefore it is necessary that we understand shirk, and also understand the connection of shirk with idol-worship, and it is also necessary to reflect on the reality of idols, and in the present age it is also necessary to discover the connection with idol-worship of the new idols which modern jahiliyyah has fashioned.

The reality is that the scope of shirk, which is the opposite of La ilaha illa Allah, extends to every situation in which, in any one aspect of life's affairs, obedience to Allah alone is absent. This state also falls within the definition of shirk: that a person, while obedient in some affairs of life, is obedient to other than Allah in other affairs. Shirk is not confined only to the outward forms of worship; those are only one particular form of shirk. In the modern age there are clear examples in our lives which show us that this is manifest shirk. A person who acknowledges Allah as One without partner, then in ablution, purity, prayer, fasting, Hajj and all other acts of worship turns towards Allah, yet alongside this, in economic dealings and collective laws, he obeys other than Allah, and in his collective values he is subject to concepts and terminologies issued by other than Allah, and in his morals, habits and customs, in his dress, he obeys those people who, in opposition to the commands of Allah, impose upon him these concepts, morals, habits and dress, which are explicitly contrary to the Shari'ah, opposed to the commands of Allah, and in reality opposed to Islam. Then this act is contrary to the testimony of faith which that person recites: La ilaha illa Allah Muhammad Rasul Allah. This is that essential matter of which the Muslims of our age are heedless. Yet this is shirk. Today's Muslims obey other than Allah in a most crude manner, and they do not perceive that this is shirk, and every age's polytheists have done exactly this.

What are idols? It is not necessary that idols be statues made of stones. Idols are in reality symbols for taghut (the tyrant or false authority), and behind these idols stands the real taghut, which, through the name and title of these idols, makes people worship it and, in the name of these idols, establishes its own servitude and system.

Idols did not speak, did not hear and did not see; in reality the custodians (mujawir) and the ruler of the time stood behind them. Some of those people used to make amulets and charms in their names, performed blowing and incantations, and in this way they kept the common masses as their slaves. Now, if in some place such symbols arise, and some institutions exist, and in the names of those institutions some priests, some religious heads and some authorities impose upon the public their concepts, their laws and their actions and dispositions, then in its reality this too will be shirk with Allah.

If nationality is made into an idol, if a homeland is made into an idol, or a state is made into an idol, or a class is made into an idol, and people are demanded to worship that idol, and to worship it in defiance of Allah, and to sacrifice for its path life, property, morals and honour, such that when the demands of these idols and the demands of the Shari'ah come into conflict, the Shari'ah of Allah, its laws and its demands are cast behind, and the demands, requirements, laws and morals of these new idols are enforced, or, to put it correctly, obedience is rendered to those worldly interests and to the tyrannical powers standing behind these new idols, then this will be manifest shirk. Such people will be idol-worshippers, polytheists, because an idol need not be a stone or wooden image; every creed and every symbol can be an idol.

Islam did not come merely to break idols made of wood and stone. The continuous hardships which the long line of the messengers of Allah endured, and the unbearable and unimaginable sufferings they bore in its cause, were not merely for the destruction of stone and wooden idols; their aim was to end every kind of idol-worship.

The reality is that Islam came precisely in order to establish a system of obedience to Allah in all matters of life. In every form and every shape, and in all matters of life, it aims to end obedience to other than Allah, whatever its form may be. Therefore, in every way and system of life, we should determine which aspect of it is tawhid and which aspect is shirk, and whether in it obedience and servitude is to Allah alone or to some other tyrannical power, some other lord or idol.

Those who consider themselves within the religion of Allah merely because they utter with their tongues the blessed testimony La ilaha illa Allah Muhammad Rasul Allah, and that too merely because they accept Allah's law in purity, the rites of worship, prayer, fasting, Hajj, marriage and divorce, or the matter of inheritance, while beyond this their whole life conforms to laws that are contrary to Allah's laws, and the majority of those laws are explicitly opposed to the Qur'an and Sunnah, and they sacrifice for those laws and that system their selves, their wealth, their morals and their culture, whether they wish it or not, and they do this so that these modern idols may be pleased with them, and the situation is such that at some stage the commands of these idols are enforced in preference to the commands and laws of Allah, then this is manifest idol-worship.

Those who consider themselves Muslims and within the religion of Allah, and whose condition is as just described, should turn back from the shirk in which they are. The religion of Islam is not the kind of thing these people imagine, those who call themselves Muslims in East and West. The religion of Islam takes in even the everyday details of life, and demands that in all the details of life obedience be rendered to Allah alone, not to speak of principles, generalities, constitution and law. This is that Islam, apart from which God does not accept any other "religion."

Shirk is not confined to a person failing to regard Allah as one; rather, the beginning of shirk is when someone regards some other than Allah as sovereign. Worshipping idols made of stones and wood is a very simple conception of idol-worship; the real idol-worship is the worship of institutions opposed to Islam.

In the simplest words, I put it thus: people should reflect on who is important in their lives? Whom do they obey completely? Whom do they obey completely? Whose following and pursuit do they adopt? Before whom do they bow in submission? If they do all these things for Allah, then they are Muslims; if they do these things for another, then they are upon that other's religion. If they are idols, then they are upon the religion of idols; if they are taghut, then they are upon the religion of taghut.

This is the message! It should be conveyed to all mankind, and they should be warned by it! They should know that Allah in this sense is One without partner! If you have intellect, then understand these things!

This is a proclamation, this is a proclamation. The truth of Allah the Mighty has been spoken.
